1 BITS-BITSoM 5-year Integrated BE-MBA Programmes: B.E. (BITS STEM Campuses in India) and MBA (BITSoM Campus) FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS Question Response General Overview 1. What is the BITS-BITSoM 5-year Integrated BE-MBA Programmes? It is a 5-year academic programme combining a 3-year of Bachelor of Engineering (B.E.) degree from BITS Pilani’s STEM campuses (India) with a 2-year Master of Business Administration (MBA) from BITSoM (BITS School of Management), Mumbai. 2. What is the aim of this programme? The programme aims to produce technology-enabled business leaders by integrating strong engineering foundations with cutting-edge business and management education. Admission Pathways 3. How can a student enter this BE+MBA dual-degree programme? There are two entry modes: • Direct Admission: Right after Class 12 through BITSAT or Board Toppers’ Scheme (starting AY 2025–26). One can directly apply through the dual degree program with effect from AY 2025-26 through BITSAT. -- 1 of 6 -- 2 Question Response • Vertical Transfer: At the end of the second year of a B.E. programme at BITS STEM campuses in India (Pilani, K K Birla Goa or Hyderabad). Continuing BE students can apply to the BITS-BITSoM 5-year Integrated BE-MBA Programmes starting June 2026. 4. Will International students be eligible? Yes, students admitted under the International Student Admissions scheme will be eligible from AY 2026–27. 5. Is an interview required for admission? • Direct Admission Pathway: No interview required. • Vertical Transfer Pathway: Yes, an application and interview are required. 6. Are students at BITS Pilani campuses other than BE students eligible to apply for Integrated BE- MBA program? • Currently only B.E. students at BITS Pilani India campuses are eligible to apply for the BITS-BITSoM 5-year Integrated BE-MBA Programmes. Eligibility Criteria 7. What is the eligibility for Direct Admission? • Admission through BITSAT/Board Toppers’/International Admission scheme. • Eligibility conditions are the same as those for the regular B.E. programme. • A minimum CGPA of 7.0 at the end of the second year is required to continue to the MBA phase at BITSoM without taking CAT. 8. What happens if a student under the Direct Admission route scores less than 7.0 CGPA by end of the second year? • They will be required to exit the programme after the third year and will not continue to the MBA phase (Please refer to response of point number 12 given below). 9. What is the eligibility for Vertical Transfer? • Students must be enrolled in a B.E. programme (with PCM input) at a BITS STEM campus. -- 2 of 6 -- 3 Question Response • A minimum CGPA of 7.0 at the end of second year. • Must apply through a separate process including an interview and SoP review. • Students with CGPA < 7.0 may still apply to BITSoM through the regular MBA admission route after completing B.E. Academic and Programme Structure 10. How is the programme structured over five years? • Years 1–3: Core engineering courses at a BITS STEM campus. • Years 4–5: Full-time residential MBA programme at BITSoM Mumbai and Open Electives requirement (Pre-defined list of courses conducted at BITSoM) of BE Programmes. 11. Will the degrees be awarded separately? • Yes. Students will receive a B.E. degree from BITS Pilani and an MBA degree from BITSoM after completion of the course work of both the degree programmes. Exit Options 12. Are there exit options from the programme? • Yes. Students who do not meet the minimum CGPA requirement of 7.0 by the end of the second year will not be eligible to continue in the integrated programme and will exit with only the B.E. degree (after completing the four- year coursework). • Additionally, any student with a CGPA below 7.0 at the end of the second year will be compulsorily exited from the integrated programme after the third year. However, such students may be permitted to continue and complete their B.E. degree, subject to their standing in the original admission merit list. • At its sole discretion, BITS Pilani may reassign such students to a different programme based on their BITSAT-2026 score and their position in the regular merit list prepared for students admitted to the First Degree Programmes -- 3 of 6 -- 4 Question Response through BITSAT-2026 (and not through the BITS-BITSoM 5-year Integrated BE- MBA Programmes). Alternatively, BITS Pilani may, subject to applicable policies, allow the credits earned in the first two years to be transferred to another recognized institute, enabling the student to pursue and complete an alternative degree of their choice. 13. Can a student choose to exit voluntarily before the MBA phase? • Yes, subject to the rules and academic progression policies that will be outlined. Discipline (programme of study of the study) may get changed depending the BITSAT score of the student and his/her admission merit position at BITS. Programme Benefits 14. What are the advantages of enrolling in this programme? • Integrated pathway into management education. • Saves one year compared to pursuing B.E. and MBA separately. • World-class faculty and curriculum at BITSoM. • Exposure to a network of industry mentors and global thought leaders. 15. Does this programme prepare students for entrepreneurship and leadership? • Yes. The programme emphasizes strategic thinking, innovation, and interdisciplinary learning, aligned with future-focused leadership development. Application and Selection 16. How will the selection process work for Direct Admission? • Students will indicate interest in the BITS-BITSoM 5-year Integrated BE-MBA Programmes at the time of Admission Preference form (29th April to 03rd June 2026). A merit list will be prepared as per availability of seats and performance in BITSAT. -- 4 of 6 -- 5 Question Response 17. How will the vertical transfer process be managed? • Details will be announced by the Dean, Admissions during the students' second year of study. It will typically involve a call for applications, evaluation of Statements of Purpose (SoPs), and interviews. Additional Information 18. Can students switch between tracks (direct and vertical)? • No. The entry modes are distinct. Students admitted via Direct Admission are expected to continue unless exiting. Vertical Transfer is an independent process. 19. Is CAT or other national MBA test required? • No, for both Direct Admission and Vertical Transfer, if students maintain a minimum CGPA of 7.0, they are exempted from CAT. 20. Is hostel accommodation provided during the MBA phase? • Yes, BITSoM is a full-time residential MBA programme located near Kalyan in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. 21. What is the fee structure for dual degree program? • The programme fees (including tuition, hostel, etc.) for the first three years will be applicable as per the BITS Pilani norms for STEM campuses in India at the respective campus. • After the successful completion of three years of the B.E. programme, students admitted to the MBA programme at BITSoM will pay the prevailing fee structure applicable to the MBA batch they are joining at BITSoM. Students enrolled in the dual degree programme will be accommodated at the BITSoM hostel during the two-year MBA programme. Accommodation and meal charges will be applicable as per the rates prevailing at the time at the BITSoM campus. 22. Does BITSoM provide accommodation during the 2-year MBA program? • Students will be accommodated at the BITSoM hostel Campus (near Mumbai) during the 2-year MBA program. -- 5 of 6 -- 6 Question Response 23 . Where can students find more information? • Detailed guidelines, FAQs, and application processes will be communicated on the official BITS Pilani and BITSoM webpage available on our admission website prior to each admission cycle. Prof. Ajit Pratap Singh Dean, Division of Admissions & Student Financial Aid (DASFA) (Institute-wide) -- 6 of 6 --

Birla Institute of Technology & Science, Pilani Vidya Vihar Pilani 333031, Rajasthan, India Tel +91 1596 255330 Fax: +91 1596 244183 Web: www.bits-pilani.ac.in Attention Public is advised not to fall prey to misinformation and fake admission offers for BITS Pilani All concerned are hereby advised not to believe in fake calls, emails and SMS regarding admissions at BITS Pilani as highlighted on our website https://admissions.bits-pilani.ac.in/. It has come to our notice that certain unscrupulous individuals/entities/agencies are approaching aspirants claiming that candidates can be admitted at BITS Pilani by paying donation money in management seats or by making false promises to help candidates clear the BITSAT exam. BITS Pilani follows the highest standard of Admissions Policy and all admission at BITS Pilani is purely on merit. We strongly advise the candidates to avoid falling prey to such deceitful practices. Those found guilty of engaging in such activities will face severe consequences, including criminal and legal actions. Please note that police complaints and FIR have been lodged against persons indulging in such malpractices. Please note that the Admissions in First Degree (B.E., M.Sc. and B.Pharm.) programmes at BITS Pilani are made by one of the following modes: 1. Admission through BITSAT Score. 2. Admission through SAT test score under International Student Admissions. 3. Admission under Board Topper Scheme. 4. Admission under 2+2 Joint Internation Collaborations (BITS-RMIT, BITS-UB, BITS-IOWA, BITS-CSP and BITS-RPI). The details of the above schemes are given at https://admissions.bits-pilani.ac.in/ Please note that we do not: 1. admit any student other than the modes specified above, 2. request payment of any kind from prospective candidates for admission other than those specified in the official admission website i.e. https://admissions.bits-pilani.ac.in/ 3. authorize anyone to either collect money or arrive at any monetary arrangement in return for admission at BITS Pilani. 4. If you receive any suspicious offers or requests from any individual/agency, please email us at admnoc@pilani.bits-pilani.ac.in BITS Pilani will initiate required criminal and legal actions against any unscrupulous individuals/entities/agencies trying to interfere in the fair and transparent conduct of BITSAT. Any parent/candidate found indulging conniving with such unscrupulous individuals/entities/agencies on monetary consideration or otherwise are also liable to face similar penal or legal actions. Also, please note that BITS Pilani shall not bear any responsibility or liability whatsoever for any loss, damage, or claims suffered by any person for acting on any unauthorized or fraudulent emails/phone calls or anyone acting on an admission offer not directly made by the Institute. Interested candidates have to apply online ensuring all deadlines are met. While applying online, candidates will be asked to give their preferences to different programmes offered. In addition, the candidate has to opt for one of the following: (i) Consideration for admission only based on GATE/GPAT score: Scores of GATE 2026 or GATE 2025 or GATE 2024 will only be considered for admissions to M.E. programmes. Similarly, scores of GPAT 2026 or GPAT 2025 or GPAT 2024 will only be considered for admission to M.Pharm. programmes. Candidates must ensure that their GATE/GPAT scores are valid and the validity as mentioned on GATE/GPAT scorecard must be quoted in the application form. (ii) Consideration for admission only on the basis of marks obtained in the BITS HD online test. (iii) Consideration for admission based on both GATE/GPAT score and marks obtained in the BITS HD online test. ▪ Details of programme-wise input eligibility criteria are given in Annexure I. ▪ Details of programme-wise eligibility through GATE / GPAT examination are given in Annexure II. ▪ Details of BITS HD Test are given in Annexure III. PREPARATION OF MERIT LIST FOR ADMISSIONS: In the process of making final admission offers to the M.E. / M.Pharm. programmes, two separate merit lists will be prepared for each programme; one based on GATE/GPAT score, and the other based on marks obtained in BITS HD test. In each program, a maximum of 50% of the seats will be filled through GATE/GPAT scores and other 50% by BITS HD test marks. The admission committee will consider a cut- off score in each category, based on the applications received and the seats available. If any seat in one category is not-filled, it will be allocated to the other category. Final decision on this will be taken by the Admissions Committee, BITS Pilani and will be binding on all. Admission to the HD programs will be on the basis of merit only. -- 6 of 55 -- Page | 4 IMPORTANT NOTE Admissions to the starred (*) M.E./M.Pharm. programs (as listed in the program table on page 2) will be made only through the BITS HD Test. Details of the BITS HD Test are given in Annexure III. Admissions will be based on students' merit rank in the BITS HD Test. FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE Candidates admitted through GATE/ GPAT will be eligible for GATE/ GPAT* scholarship provided by AICTE/PCI. Institute will facilitate the submission of documents to AICTE/PCI for scholarships. In addition, candidates admitted through GATE/ GPAT* route will be eligible for a tuition fee waiver amounting to Rs. 13,400/- per month (during the semester) over and above the GATE / GPAT* scholarship. Candidates admitted through the BITS HD Test route will be eligible for a stipend of Rs. 13,400/- per month (during the semester). All the candidates who will be receiving fee waiver or stipend will need to contribute to graduate student teaching assistantship of 8 -10 hours of work per week. Consideration for fellowship will be as per Institute norms. * GPAT Scholarship is exclusively applicable to students admitted to the Pilani Campus only. APPLICATION PROCESS 1. Computer based online test means the candidate sits in front of a computer, the questions are presented on the computer monitor, and the candidate submits the answers using keyboard & mouse. Each computer is connected to a server, which prepares the question set and delivers to the candidate on the computer. The online tests will be conducted on 25th May & 26th May 2026 and the candidates can choose the Center to take the test as mentioned in later sections. A. DETAILS OF THE ONLINE TEST Test I: Duration: 45 Minutes Total No of questions: 30 Test I is compulsory for all students who are applying for any of the Higher Degree programs of the Institute and will consist of the following sections: Sections No. of Questions Core Mathematics 15 English Language Skills & Logical Reasoning 15 Total 30 The course descriptions are available in the syllabus given later in the brochure. Test II: Duration: 105 Minutes Total number of questions: 70 Test II is for students applying to all Higher Degree programs except those who are applying for M.E. in Environmental Engineering and M.E. in Software systems. This paper will attempt to test the student’s grasp of the basic subjects of his/her discipline. The discipline courses of different degree programmes of BITS have been used for constructing the questions. The course descriptions are available in the syllabus given later in the brochure. Test for Software Systems: Duration: 60 Minutes Total number of questions: 50 This special test for Software Systems is required for only those students who are applying for M.E. Software systems. The course description is available in the syllabus given later in the brochure. Test for M.E. Environmental Engineering Duration: 60 Minutes Total number of questions: 50 This special test for Environmental Engineering is required for only those students who are applying for M.E. Environmental Engineering. The course description is available in the syllabus given later in the brochure. For all the above tests, the questions are of objective type (multiple-choice questions); each question with four answer choices, only one being the correct choice. Each correct answer fetches 3 marks, while each incorrect answer has a penalty of 1 mark. No marks are awarded or deducted for questions not attempted. While the candidate can skip a question, the computer will not allow the candidate to choose -- 15 of 55 -- Page | 13 more than one option as the correct answer. All the questions and instructions for the test will be in English only. The questions will be selected at random from a large question bank. Different candidates will get different question sets. An expert committee will ensure that the question sets are of comparable difficulty level, content, question type etc. In this matter, the decision of the expert committee will be final and binding on the candidate. B. TEST CENTER DETAILS** The planned HD test centers are in the following cities. The final list of centers and the operating days at each center will depend on the number of applicants and their preferences. Composition 4.1 Rearrangement 4.2 Paragraph Unity 4.3 Linkers/Connectives (b) Logical Reasoning The test is given to the candidates to judge their power of reasoning spread in verbal and nonverbal areas. The candidates should be able to think logically so that they perceive the data accurately, understand the relationships correctly, figure out the missing numbers or words, and to apply rules to new and different contexts. These indicators are measured through performance on such tasks as detecting missing links, following directions, classifying words, establishing sequences, and completing analogies. 5. Verbal Reasoning 5.1 Analogy Analogy means correspondence. In the questions based on analogy, a particular relationship is given and another similar relationship has to be identified from the alternatives provided. 5.2 Classification Classification means to assort the items of a given group on the basis of certain common quality they possess and then spot the odd option out. 5.3 Series Completion Here series of numbers or letters are given and one is asked to either complete the series or find out the wrong part in the series. 5.4 Logical Deduction – Reading Passage -- 20 of 55 -- Page | 18 Here a brief passage is given and based on the passage the candidate is required to identify the correct or incorrect logical conclusions. 5.5 Chart Logic Here a chart or a table is given that is partially filled in and asks to complete it in accordance with the information given either in the chart / table or in the question. 6. Nonverbal Reasoning 6.1 Pattern Perception Here a certain pattern is given and generally a quarter is left blank. The candidate is required to identify the correct quarter from the given four alternatives. 6.2 Figure Formation and Analysis The candidate is required to analyze and form a figure from various given parts. 6.3 Paper Cutting It involves the analysis of a pattern that is formed when a folded piece of paper is cut into a definite design. 6.4 Figure Matrix In this more than one set of figures is given in the form of a matrix, all of them following the same rule. The candidate is required to follow the rule and identify the missing figure. 6.5 Rule Detection Here a particular rule is given and it is required to select from the given sets of figures, a set of figures, which obeys the rule and forms the correct series. -- 21 of 55 -- Page | 19 SYLLABUS FOR TEST II Chemical Engineering Chemical Process Calculations Chemical Process Calculations: Units and Dimensions, Chemical Equation and Stoichiometry, Thermodynamic properties of Gases, Vapors, Liquids and Solids, Steady and unsteady state mass and energy balances, Phase Equilibria (multiphase, multicomponent), reacting and non-reacting systems, recycle, bypass and purge calculations, Combustion Calculations. BIRLA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY & SCIENCE (BITS), PILANI SCHEDULE OF FEES# The following are the details of the fees in INR payable by all students admitted to Higher Degree Programmes for the academic year, 2026-27 at BITS Pilani. FEES Pilani Campus Goa Campus Hyderabad Campus Admission Fees * 64,100/- 64,100/- 64,100/- Semester/Term Fees First Semester * 2,91,500/- 2,91,500/- 2,91,500/- Second Semester 2,91,500/- 2,91,500/- 2,91,500/- Summer term 1,02,000/- 1,02,000/- 1,02,000/- Students' Union fee * 450/- 450/- 450/- Students' Aid Fund * 225/- 225/- 225/- Hostel fee (for on-campus students only) First Semester * 36,000/- 36,000/- 36,000/- Second Semester 36,000/- 36,000/- 36,000/- Summer term 18,000/- 18,000/- 18,000/- Mess & Electricity advance First Semester * 10,000/- 10,000/- 10,000/- Second Semester 10,000/- 10,000/- 10,000/- Summer term 5,000/- 5,000/- 5,000/- (Payable at the beginning of each semester/term and adjustable at the end of the same) Other Advances First Semester * 12,000/- 12,000/- 12,000/- Second Semester 12,000/- 12,000/- 12,000/- (Payable at the beginning of each semester/term and adjustable at the end of the same) Institute Caution Deposit * 3,000/- 3,000/- 3,000/- # Changes (if any), will be notified here on this page. * Payable at the time of admission Notes: 1. Students admitted in AY 2026-27 will pay a tuition fee of 2,91,500/- per Semester in AY 2026- 27. In subsequent years (AY 2027-28, 2028-29 etc.), tuition fee will increase @5% every year in INR for 2026-27 batch students (unless the government announces any new levy/tax, which will be passed onto all existing students irrespective of their year of entry). In addition, hostel fee will be increased every year. 2. Additional fees will also apply, should a student registers for practice school in a semester (i.e. 35% of the semester fee of the previous academic year in INR). 3. For some specific programmes requiring special treatment, fees and mode of their payment will be determined by the Vice-Chancellor in consultation with the Chancellor. -- 1 of 1 --

OF MANAGEMENT BITS PILANI, PILANI CAMPUS HOD'S MESSAGE -- 4 of 39 -- ABOUT THE INSTITUTE 02 The Birla Institute of Technology & Science (BITS) Pilani is one of India's leading higher education institutes and a deemed university under Sec. 3 of the UGC Act 1956. The institute has been recognized as an "Institution of Eminence" by MHRD. The primary motive of BITS is to train young men and women able and eager to create and put into action ideas, methods, techniques, and information. Over the years, BITS Pilani has provided the highest quality technical education to students from all across India admitted on the basis of merit & a critical selection process. Its graduates may be found throughout the world in all areas of engineering, science, humanities, and management. Academic Curriculum at BITS is continuously being innovated and refreshed to reflect the latest developments in technology and match the trends within the industry. Pure academics are supplemented by persuasive industry engagement and every student is exposed to practical applications of classroom knowledge under a structured semester-long engagement programme. The institute is committed to generating, disseminating, and preserving knowledge, and to working with others to bring this knowledge to tackle the challenges facing the world. -- 5 of 39 -- ABOUT DEPARTMENT OF MANAGEMENT 03 To advance management knowledge and develop impactful leaders. The Department of Management (earlier known as the management group) at BITS Pilani was established in the year 1971. It initially offered two years' Master of Business Administration (MBA). In 1973 MBA evolved into the integrated first-degree programme MMS (Master of Management Studies) which was a blend of engineering and management. The objective of this programme is to bridge the gap in the industry by providing quality management professionals with strong technical skills and acumen for managing a business. Based on demands from the industry, the course was restructured again as MBA in 2006. It is a two-year Post-Graduate Programme for graduates who wish to pursue their career in management. Catering to the contemporary industry demands, BITS Pilani has introduced an MBA in Business Analytics from the academic year 2021-22. BITS Pilani has been ranked 7th in the university category in India as per NIRF 2025. The MBA program in BITS Pilani is among the top-25 in the country as per The Week HANSA 2024 report. BITS Pilani is in the 451-500 band globally for Business and Management Studies by QS World University Ranking by Subject (2025). EVOLUTION & MILESTONES OF BITS MBA To be the destination of first choice for key stakeholders viz. students, faculty, organizations and community community by designing and delivering cutting-edge management programme in a learning environment that develops leaders who are socially responsible, innovative & result oriented. VISION MISSION -- 6 of 39 -- MBA IN BUSINESS ANALYTICS PROGRAM 04 MBA in Business Analytics is a two-year full-time residential programme aimed at creating business analytics professionals employable by leading Indian and foreign firms. The programme integrates technology with statistical and quantitative modeling techniques to provide students with the foundation needed for data-driven decision making, as well as for graduate study in the field of Business Analytics. The focus of this programme is on the application of analytics and Technology in all the functional areas of management, including but not limited to, marketing, finance, operations, human resources, entrepreneurship, etc. The curriculum balances a depth of analytical training with a breadth of business knowledge. This programme is designed for those who have an analytical mindset, and interested in tackling challenging business problems. The major perks of the on-campus MBA in Business Analytics programme: Develop awareness of the descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive modeling comprising Business Analytics. Have a strategic understanding of business analytics and business disciplines to make holistic judgments when analyzing business situations. Apply deep analytical skills, business knowledge, and critical problem-solving expertise to efficiently and effectively transform data into sound business decisions that give a competitive edge. -- 7 of 39 -- HIGHLIGHTS OF THE PROGRAM 05 BITS Pilani has been ranked 7th in the university category in India as per NIRF 2025. BITS Pilani is in the 451-500 band globally for Business and Management Studies by QS World University Ranking by Subject (2025). Two year on-campus programme benchmarked with the best in the world Top class faculty with doctoral and post-doctoral experience Legendary alumni network World class infrastructure in a lush green campus One to one mentoring programme and continuous interaction with industry leaders Option of six months’ structured and paid internship Paid teaching assistantship opportunity -- 8 of 39 -- OVERVIEW OF THE PROGRAM 06 ACADEMICS The curriculum of MBA in Business Analytics is globally benchmarked with the leading Business Analytics programme across the globe and is vetted by industry practitioners. Lectures supplemented by case studies and software tools are carried out in all the courses which enhance students analytical, problem solving, and decision- making skills. This facilitates active learning among the students as they face real business issues, apply their classroom knowledge, and strengthen their business acumen. An intellectually stimulating learning environment is provided by our well-qualified and experienced faculty. Students can also pursue Off-campus Thesis/Semester Abroad programmes in foreign universities/ institutes ranked in the first 400 by QS and Time Higher Education. SKILL-BASED LEARNING The Department of Management facilitates the students to earn certification in 21st-century industry-relevant skills such as Design Thinking, Data Visualization, and Project Management Practitioner (PMP). To cater to the expectations of Generation Z students, the department has created the Personality Improvement, Leadership Orientation and Teamwork (P.I.L.O.T.) programme to provide customized learning experiences according to their needs factoring in their areas of skill gap, learning preferences, and future professional choices. ALUMNI The Mentorship Programme for MBA in Business Analytics is a unique initiative by the Department of Management at BITS Pilani to impart industry-relevant skills to the students in collaboration with the BITS Alumni Association. Under this programme, management students are given an opportunity to interact and be mentored by BITS alumni experienced in the Analytics domain. Alumni are also frequently called for invited talks to share industry insights with the students. INDUSTRY CONNECT At the end of their second semester, students go on a two-month integrated industry exposure in the form of summer internships in reputed organizations. All students also have the opportunity to enroll for 6 months of structured Practice School, as a part of the curriculum. In addition, the webinar series organized by the department invites eminent guests from the industry on a regular basis. These guests having huge experience and unparalleled expertise come from varied industries and diverse countries, contributing to student learning. -- 9 of 39 -- CURRICULUM 07 Introduction to Syllabus for Business Analytics Aptitude Test The Business Analytics Aptitude Test (BAAT) for admission to the Two-Year (On-Campus) MBA in Business Analytics in the Academic Year 2026-27 will comprise of a) Management Aptitude Section and b) Analytics Aptitude Section. The total duration of BAAT examination is 3 hours. All the questions are multiple choice-based questions. The syllabus and pattern are as follows: a) Management Aptitude Section: This section will measure management aptitude in three areas– Quantitative Ability, Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension and Data Interpretation & Logical Reasoning. Verbal Ability: Verbal Reasoning, Sentence completion, Grammar, Syllogisms, Jumbled paragraphs, Para Completion and inference, Contextual usage, Foreign language words used in English, Reading Comprehension, Analogies, Sentence correction, Verbal Logic, Different usage of same word, Idioms, Parajumbles, Antonyms. Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning: Blood Relations, Series, Proposition, Direction Sense, Coding-Decoding, Assumptions, Puzzles, Clocks and Calendars, Statements, Data Arrangement, Family Tree, Binary Logic, Seating Arrangement, Sets & Caselets, Syllogism, Venn Diagram, Data Structures, Tables & Pie Charts, Data Sufficiency, Bars & Line Graphs. Quantitative Aptitude: Geometry, Trigonometry, Algebra, Mensuration, Partnership (Accounts), Profit & Loss, Ratios and Proportion, In-equations Quadratic and linear equations, Surds and Indices, Time- Speed-Distance, Number System, Geometric Progression, Inequalities, Work and Time, Percentages, Logarithms. b) Analytics Aptitude Section: The objective of the analytics aptitude test is to check candidate’s basic aptitude on computers and mathematics. The questions will be of multiple choice from Matrices; Linear Algebra; Coordinate geometry in two dimensions, Basic Differential and Integral Calculus; Numerical Analysis; Probability and combination; Fundamental Programming Concepts; Basic Data Structures (arrays, lists, stacks, and queues); Boolean Algebra. -- 1 of 1 --

Sample Questions for the Business Analytics Aptitude Test (2026) Section 1 (Management Aptitude Section) 1. The new vaccine can be administered to all, to those under 18. a) Accept b) Except c) Expect d) Access 2. Arrange the following words in a meaningful sequence: 1. Tree, 2. Branch, 3. Leaf, 4. Forest, 5. Woods. a) 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 b) 3, 2, 1, 4, 5 c) 3, 2, 1, 5, 4 d) 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 3. In each of the following questions find out the alternative which will best replace the question mark. Flock : Bird :: ? : Wolf a) Group b) Pack c) Bunch d) Herd 4. Choose the word which is different from the rest. a) Electron b) Neutron c) Proton d) Radon 5. Identify the incorrect usage of the term ‘pass’. a) Pass on the salt please. b) He passed the test with flying colors. c) I am a 2020 pass out MBA. d) Her father sadly passed away last week. 6. Choose the option which is opposite to the meaning of ‘pertinent’ a) Germane b) Irrelevant c) Impertinent d) Impatient 7. Spot the error in the following: (1) The reason why he is rejected (2) is because (3) he is unexperienced. (4) No error a) 1 b) 2 c) 3 d) 4 -- 1 of 14 -- 8. When someone explains the events in order of their occurrence, it is called a/an a) Anthology b) Chronology c) Ontology d) Theology 9. Arrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph. P. According to the residents, the name of the town comes from the name of the famous Jat warrior, who belonged to the Pilania gotra. Q. It is said that the warrior courageously fought and sacrificed his life to protect a fort in the town from invasion by enemies. R. Pilani is a small town lying in the Shekhawati region of Rajasthan. S. Currently the town is most notably famous for Birla Institute of Technology & Science, and for Central Electronics Engineering Research Institute. T. A vaccine is a substance that is introduced into the body to prevent infection or to control disease due to a certain pathogen, which is a disease-causing organism, such as a virus, bacteria or parasite. The vaccine “teaches” the body how to defend itself against the pathogen by creating an immune response. Preventive vaccines work to protect an individual from infection or disease by introducing a small component or a non- harmful form of the pathogen (called the foreign antigen) into the body. The body produces an immune response to the pathogen by generating antibodies (via the humoral response), killer cells (via the cell- mediated response), or both. A small group of memory B-cells and T-cells remain in the body and can quickly initiate a strong immune response, i.e., by producing antibodies, and helping the production of killer T-cells or antibodies, respectively. The next time the real pathogen is encountered, the immune system remembers it and mounts a much larger, quicker response than it would have if the individual had never received the vaccine. This is known as “immune memory”. 11. What are the examples of pathogens? a) Bacteria b) Parasite c) Virus d) All of the above 12. Frequently Asked Questions Applicable for Admission to the Two-year Full Time On-Campus MBA in Business Analytics Program: Academic Year 2026-27 BITS Pilani (Pilani Campus) Application Stage Query: • What is the eligibility criteria for admission to the MBA in Business Analytics program? Candidates must hold a bachelor's degree of a minimum three years duration in any discipline or its equivalent. A minimum of 60% aggregate marks is required in the qualifying degree. Candidates must have studied at least one subject in Mathematics or Statistics at the high school level (10+2) or higher. Students in the final year of their qualifying degree program are also eligible to apply, provided they can submit original copies of their results by 1st October 2026. Exposure to a programming language is desirable but not mandatory. Candidates will be required to appear for the Business Analytics Aptitude Test (BAAT) conducted by BITS Pilani. Final selection will be based on overall performance in: 1. Business Analytics Aptitude Test (BAAT) 2. Personal Interview 3. CAT (2025) / XAT (2026) / GMAT (2025) scores (if available) 4. Prior work experience (if any) 5. Previous academic history Note: Meeting the minimum eligibility does not guarantee admission into the program. • Is there any minimum percentage of marks that I should have obtained in mathematics or statistics at the high school (10+2) or higher level? The eligibility criteria do not specify a minimum percentage of marks that must be obtained in Mathematics or Statistics at the high school (10+2) or higher level. Candidates are required to have studied at least one subject in Mathematics or Statistics, but the focus is on having the subject in their academic background rather than a specific percentage. It is advisable to check with the admissions office/department for any updates or specific requirements related to this aspect. • Is it mandatory to appear for CAT / XAT / GMAT to be considered for admission to the MBA in Business Analytics program? It is not mandatory to appear for CAT (Common Admission Test), XAT (Xavier Aptitude Test), or GMAT (Graduate Management Admission Test) to be considered for admission to the MBA in Business Analytics program. However, if candidates have taken CAT, XAT, or GMAT, their scores may be considered as part of the selection process. Candidates are required to appear for the Business Analytics Aptitude Test (BAAT) conducted by BITS Pilani. -- 1 of 11 -- In summary, while CAT/XAT/GMAT scores can enhance a candidate's application, they are not a mandatory requirement for admission. • I am in the final year of my Qualifying Degree. How should I calculate my CGPA / Percentage? If you are in the final year of your qualifying degree program, you can apply for admission provided you meet the eligibility criteria. Convert your grades into the CGPA format as per your institution's grading system. Typically, CGPA is calculated by taking the sum of the grade points earned in all subjects and dividing it by the total number of credits. If your institution provides a percentage, you can use that directly. If you need to convert CGPA to percentage, the formula may vary by institution. Ensure to check your institution's specific conversion formula if available. If selected/offered admission, you must submit the original copies of your results by 1st October 2026 to confirm your eligibility. It is advisable to consult your institution's guidelines for the exact method of calculation and any specific requirements for reporting your CGPA or percentage. • Is the CGPA / percentage for entire Qualifying Degree program considered for admission or only the final year is considered? The admission process considers the CGPA or percentage obtained throughout the entire qualifying degree program, not just the final year. If you are in the final year, you will need to provide your cumulative performance up to that point, which includes all semesters or years completed. You must have a minimum of 60% aggregate marks in your qualifying degree to be eligible for admission. In summary, the entire academic performance across the qualifying degree program is taken into account for the admission process. • My university mentions the CGPA / percentage for only the final year in the final mark-sheet. Should I still report the CGPA / percentage for entire program while applying for the MBA in Business Analytics program? • The application requires an overall CGPA or percentage for the entire qualifying degree program, you may need to calculate it based on the grades from all previous years and semesters, if available. • I have not yet completed my Qualifying Degree and till now my CGPA / percentage is below 60%. I expect my final aggregate CGPA / percentage to be more than 60%. Can I apply for the MBA in Business Analytics program? Yes, you may apply for the MBA in Business Analytics program. However, once you finish your Qualifying Degree, you should have obtained a minimum of 60% aggregate marks in all the semesters/years combined. Otherwise, any offer of admission to the MBA in Business Analytics program of the institute will stand cancelled whenever you are found to have scored below 60% aggregate marks in your Qualifying Degree. • My university calculates CGPA on a scale that is not 10-pointer (e.g. 7 pointer or 9 pointer). Shall I report CGPA in that scale only or convert it to a 10-pointer scale? You should convert the CGPA to a percentage on a 10-pointer scale. -- 2 of 11 -- • How can I convert my CGPA to a 10-pointer scale, if my university reports it on another scale? If your university has specific guidelines for conversion, it is advisable to follow those. To convert your CGPA to a 10-point scale, you can use the following formula: For a 7-point scale: (Your CGPA / 7) * 10 For a 9-point scale: (Your CGPA / 9) * 10 Ensure to indicate the original scale and the converted scale if required. When filling out your application, report the converted CGPA along with a note indicating the original scale and the conversion process used. • Do I need to get hard copies of my certificates attested by a gazetted officer or will self-attestation suffice? Self-attestation of your certificates is sufficient for the application process. This means you can sign and date the copies of your documents to confirm that they are true copies of the originals. It is advisable to check the specific requirements mentioned in the admission guidelines or application instructions provided by BITS Pilani. • Can I transfer application fee through my bank to the account of BITS Pilani? If yes, please provide the bank account details. No. You need to choose from the list of acceptable modes of payment mentioned in the online application form. Bank account transfer is not accepted. Check the MBA Business Analytics brochure or contact the admissions office directly via email or phone to request the most accurate and updated bank account details, if needed. • Can I pay the application fee by cash? No, cash is not accepted. BITS Pilani does not accept cash payments for the application fee. It is essential to refer to the official admission guidelines or the application portal for specific instructions regarding payment methods. If you have further questions or need clarification, it is advisable to contact the admissions office directly. • How long will it take to get refund in case I have paid multiple times because of technical faults? BITS Pilani tries best to resolve such issues at the earliest. However, because of certain technical and operational issues the time may vary for different students. The time it takes to process a refund for duplicate application fee payments due to technical faults can vary. Typically, it may take anywhere from a few days to a few weeks. You should promptly notify the admissions office about the duplicate payment, providing details such as transaction IDs and payment receipts. Ensure to follow any specific procedures outlined by BITS Pilani for requesting a refund. Keep in mind that the actual refund may also depend on your bank's processing time once the refund is initiated by BITS Pilani. • Can I get refund of application fee if I am found to be ineligible for the MBA in Business Analytics program or if I am not shortlisted for the second round of the admission process (i.e. personal interviews)? Application fees are non-refundable, even if a candidate is found to be ineligible for the MBA in Business Analytics program. Similarly, if a candidate is not shortlisted for the -- 3 of 11 -- second round of the admission process (personal interviews), the application fee is not refunded. It is important to refer to the official admission guidelines or the application portal for specific details regarding the refund policy. For any clarifications or specific inquiries regarding the refund of the application fee, it is advisable to contact the admissions office directly. • Is there any type of quota for admission to the MBA in Business Analytics program? Admission is only based on merit. It is advisable to check the official admission guidelines for detailed information regarding merit-based admissions for the MBA in Business Analytics program. • When can I get the confirmation of my payment of application fee? Upon successful payment, you should receive a payment receipt via email or through the application portal. Ensure to check your spam or junk folder if you do not see the confirmation in your inbox. Typically, you can expect to receive confirmation of your application fee payment shortly after the transaction is processed. This may take anywhere from a few minutes to a few hours, depending on the payment method used. You can also log into your application portal to verify the status of your payment. There may be a section that indicates whether your application fee has been successfully processed. If you do not receive confirmation within a reasonable time frame, or if you encounter any issues, it is advisable to contact the admissions office for assistance. • From where can I get to know the important deadlines for MBA in Business Analytics admission-related activities? Please check the website for BITS Pilani Admission. The most reliable source for important deadlines related to the admission process is the official BITS Pilani admissions website. If you have already registered on the application portal, it may provide updates and notifications regarding deadlines and other admission-related activities. Keep an eye on your email for any communications from BITS Pilani regarding important deadlines and updates related to the admission process. • Do I need to provide any proof of work experience while applying? While applying for the MBA in Business Analytics program at BITS Pilani, you may be required to provide proof of work experience that verifies your employment and duration of service if you have any. If you are a fresher and do not have any work experience, you do not need to provide proof of work experience. • I could not download the application form. What can I do? (Max. 300 words) o What do you expect to learn while pursuing MBA in Business Analytics? (Max. 300 words) o What makes you a suitable candidate for an MBA in Business Analytics? (Max. 300 words) • What is the Syllabus and pattern for Business Analytics Aptitude Test (BAAT)? The BAAT will comprise of a) Management Aptitude Section and b) Analytics Aptitude Section. The total duration of the test is 3 hours, and there is no sectional time limit. The syllabus and pattern is as follows: a) Management Aptitude Section: This section will measure management aptitude in three areas– Quantitative Ability, Verbal Ability & Reading Comprehension and Data Interpretation & Logical Reasoning. The questions will be multiple choice. Verbal Ability: Verbal Reasoning, Sentence completion, Grammar, Syllogisms, Jumbled paragraphs, Para Completion and inference, Contextual usage, Foreign language words used in English, Reading Comprehension, Analogies, Sentence correction, Verbal Logic, Different usage of same word, Idioms, Parajumbles, Antonyms. Data Interpretation and Logical Reasoning: Blood Relations, Series, Proposition, Direction Sense, Coding-Decoding, Assumptions, Puzzles, Clocks and Calendars, Statements, Data Arrangement, Family Tree, Binary Logic, Seating Arrangement, Sets & Caselets, Syllogism, Venn Diagram, Data Structures, Tables & Pie Charts, Data Sufficiency, Bars & Line Graphs. Quantitative Aptitude: Geometry, Trigonometry, Algebra, Mensuration, Partnership (Accounts), Profit & Loss, Ratios and Proportion, In-equations Quadratic and linear equations, Surds and Indices, Time-Speed-Distance, Number System, Geometric Progression, Inequalities, Work and Time, Percentages, Logarithms. b) Analytics Aptitude Section: The objective of the analytics aptitude test is to check candidate’s basic aptitude on computers and mathematics. The questions will be of multiple choice from Matrices; Linear Algebra; Coordinate geometry in two dimensions, Basic Differential and Integral Calculus; Numerical Analysis; Probability and combination; Fundamental Programming Concepts; Basic Data Structures (arrays, lists, stacks, and queues); Boolean Algebra. -- 6 of 11 -- • What is the marking scheme for the Business Analytics Aptitude Test (BAAT)? Each correct answer will be awarded 3 marks and each wrong answer will result in deduction of 1 mark. No marks are awarded for questions not attempted. • How can I rectify any error, which I made during the application process? BAAT and Personal Interview Stage Query: • What are the different stages in the selection process? The admission process comprises the following steps: Step 1: Candidates will apply for admission by filling the application form. Step 2: Applicants' eligibility status will be verified through the application form. Step 3: Applicants satisfying the eligibility criteria will be called for the Business Analytics Aptitude Test (BAAT), which comprises of Management Aptitude Section and Analytics Aptitude Section. Step 4: Applicants will be shortlisted for Personal Interview (PI) based on their performance in BAAT. The institute will decide the cut-off marks for BAAT. Step 5: Final selection will be based on overall performance in i) Business Analytics Aptitude Test, ii) Personal Interview & iii) CAT/XAT/GMAT (if available), along with prior work experience, and previous academic history. A certain weightage will be given to candidates having good percentile in CAT / XAT / GMAT. • How does BITS Pilani evaluate a candidate before making offer for provisional admission? The offers for provisional admission will be made based on following evaluation parameters. The term fee refers to the fee charged for a specific academic term or semester in a program. It covers various costs associated with the educational services provided during that period. A term fee is applicable for a defined duration, typically corresponding to a semester (e.g., first semester, second semester) or a specific academic term (e.g., summer term). • Do I need to pay admission fee in each semester or year of my study? Academic Graduate Studies and Research Division BITS Pilani A Candidate seeking “Part-Time” admission should: Work in an organization which encourages and facilitates research. Meet the requisite minimum qualification for admission to Ph.D program of BITS Pilani. Have a minimum of one year work experience in related field. Furnish a "Consent & No Objection Certificate" from his/her parent organization in a prescribed format (provided at the end of this document) Minimum eligibility criteria for admissions: M.E./M.Tech./M.Pharm./MBA/M.Phil. or an equivalent Degree with a minimum of 60% aggregate in the qualifying examination. M.Sc./B.E./B.Pharm. or an equivalent degree with a minimum of 60% aggregate in the qualifying examination For admissions to Humanities and Social Sciences, candidates with an M.A. degree and a minimum of 55% aggregate may apply. Meeting the minimum eligibility criteria does not guarantee admission into the PhD program. In addition, Departments may set specific admission criteria for shortlisting. Shortlisted candidates will have to appear for an admission test, which may comprise of a written exam and/or interview. Candidates admitted with qualifications like M.Sc., B.E., B.Pharm., M.A. etc., will be required to do course work on admission to the program. Not all Departments across the campuses of BITS Pilani are likely to admit 'Part-time' students. Department’s Preference with regard to the “Part-Time” student admission into the General admission information and the PhD admission brochure are available at “PhD_Brochure (bitsadmission.com)” Financial Assistance: Financial assistance is not provided to the candidates under PhD (Part Time) program. It is mandatory for interested part-time candidates to obtain all necessary permissions from his/her employer. Admission will be made by following the same process of selection as that for full- time candidates. All existing academic regulations that apply to full-time students admitted to the Doctoral program will also be applicable to part-time PhD students, unless specifically mentioned otherwise. Information related to Part-Time Admission Doctoral program is available in the PhD admission brochure. -- 1 of 2 -- PhD course work for Part-time candidates: Course work is decided by the Department based on the background of the candidate and whether he or she will work in an area of research different from his background. Candidates may contact the respective Department HOD for required information. The number of courses to be taken will again depend on the background and/or area of research of the candidate. General guidelines for coursework may be noted as given below: (i) A candidate having an Undergraduate Degree equivalent to the First Degree of BITS Pilani i.e. BE, BPharm or MSc. will need to do coursework which typically is spread across 2 Semesters. (ii) A candidate having a Higher Degree equivalent of BITS Pilani like ME, MPharm, MBA etc. may need to do coursework of one or two semester duration (to be decided by the concerned Department at the time of interview). In both cases, the courses offered will be at the discretion of the Department. Coursework will have to be done on campus. Off-campus coursework is not permitted. *Format for obtaining “Consent & No Objection Certificate” from employer (To be submitted on official stationery of organization along with application form) This is to certify that Mr./Ms.............................................. is working in our organization as.................................................since.............. The Organization has no objection if Mr./Ms..................... ........................ is admitted to part-time PhD programme of BITS Pilani. The organization will grant leave as and when required and all necessary facilities to the employee in order to complete all components of PhD programme. Date: Signature of Head of the organization with Seal -- 2 of 2 --

1 AFFIDAVIT-CUM-DECLARATION AND INDEMNITY BOND (For Scholarship / Fee Waiver / Financial Assistance) (To be executed on a ₹100/- Non-Judicial Stamp Paper and duly notarized, if you have been selected for upfront Merit-cum-Need Scholarship or Tuition Blind scheme) I, Mr./Ms. ____________________________, S/o/D/o ____________________________, BITSAT-2026 Application No. ____________________, having been offered admission to Integrated First Degree Programme at Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani ("BITS Pilani" / "Institute")_______________Campus, together with my Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s), namely: 1. Mr./Mrs. ____________________________ 2. Mr./Mrs. ____________________________ do hereby solemnly affirm, declare and undertake as follows: 1. I/We have applied for scholarship, fee waiver, financial assistance, concession or other financial benefit offered by the Institute ("Scholarship") and understand that grant of such benefit is subject to fulfillment of the eligibility criteria prescribed by the Institute from time to time. -- 1 of 3 -- 2 2. For the purpose of Scholarship eligibility, "Family Income" shall mean the aggregate gross annual income of the Student's Father and Mother from all sources. Where eligibility is based on a Legal Guardian, it shall mean the aggregate gross annual income of such Legal Guardian(s). 3. I/We declare that all information, declarations, Income Tax Returns, income certificates, salary records, financial statements and other documents submitted to the Institute in support of the Scholarship application are true, complete, genuine and accurate. 4. I/We specifically declare that the Income Tax Returns for Assessment Year(s) 2025-26 and all supporting financial documents submitted to the Institute are authentic, validly issued and have not been forged, fabricated, manipulated, altered, procured by misrepresentation or otherwise unlawfully obtained. 5. I/We further declare that all sources of income of the Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s), including salary, business income, professional income, consultancy income, rental income, agricultural income, investment income, pension, foreign income and any other income whatsoever, have been fully and truthfully disclosed to the Institute and that no material financial information has been concealed, omitted or suppressed. 6. I/We acknowledge and undertake that the Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s) whose names appear in the income documents submitted at the time of admission shall continue to form the basis for determining the Student's eligibility for scholarship throughout the Student's tenure at the Institute. The Student shall, however, be required to submit the latest income documents of the same Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s) at the beginning of each semester to the Student Welfare Division of the respective campus for assessment of the Student's scholarship eligibility. The Institute shall not permit the substitution or replacement of such Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s) with any other person for the purpose of determining the Student's scholarship eligibility. 7. I/We acknowledge and agree that Scholarship eligibility shall be reviewed by the Institute from time to time in accordance with the applicable Scholarship policy. I/We undertake to submit, at my/our own responsibility, the prescribed Income Tax Returns, income certificates, declarations and such other financial documents as may be required by the Institute for each academic year or at such intervals as may be prescribed by the Institute. Failure to submit the required documents within the prescribed timeline may result in withholding, discontinuance or withdrawal of the Scholarship and, if any Scholarship amount or financial benefit has already been granted on a provisional basis, the same shall be liable to be recovered by the Institute. 8. I/We acknowledge and agree that grant, continuation, renewal, enhancement, reduction, suspension or withdrawal of any Scholarship, fee waiver, financial assistance, concession or other financial benefit shall be solely at the discretion of the Institute and subject to the applicable rules, policies, eligibility criteria and conditions prescribed by the Institute from time to time. I/We further confirm that I/we have read and understood the applicable Scholarship terms and conditions and that no Scholarship or financial assistance shall be claimed as a matter of right. The Institute shall be entitled to discontinue or withdraw the Scholarship upon the Student ceasing to satisfy any prescribed eligibility condition or upon occurrence of any event under the applicable rules or policies of the Institute including, without limitation, disciplinary action, misconduct, submission of incorrect information, failure to submit prescribed documents, or failure to satisfy the applicable financial or minimum academic eligibility criteria. 9. I/We expressly authorize the Institute, at any stage before admission, during the programme, after graduation, after issuance of any academic credential, or at any subsequent time, to verify or cause verification of any declaration, Income Tax Return, certificate, financial document or supporting record submitted in connection with the Scholarship application from any authority, employer, institution, bank, financial institution or other source considered appropriate by the Institute. 10. If at any stage it is found that any declaration, Income Tax Return, certificate or supporting document is false, forged, fabricated, misleading, incomplete, manipulated, or that any material income or financial -- 2 of 3 -- 3 information has been concealed or suppressed, or that the Student was otherwise not eligible for the Scholarship, the Institute shall be entitled to withdraw or cancel the Scholarship, recover the entire financial benefit granted, demand payment of the applicable fees and charges, and initiate such disciplinary, civil, criminal or other proceedings as may be permissible under applicable law and the rules, policies and regulations of the Institute.The aforesaid rights of the Institute may be exercised irrespective of whether such discrepancy, concealment, misrepresentation or ineligibility is discovered before admission, during the course of study, after graduation, or after issuance of any academic credential. 11. I/We jointly and severally agree to indemnify and keep indemnified BITS Pilani, its campuses, officers, employees and representatives against all losses, claims, liabilities, damages, costs and expenses arising out of any false declaration, forged document, concealment of income, misrepresentation or wrongful receipt of Scholarship benefits. 12. I/We agree that any amount determined by the Institute to be recoverable under this Affidavit-cum- Declaration and Indemnity Bond shall constitute a lawful debt due to the Institute and shall remain recoverable notwithstanding completion of studies, withdrawal from the programme, graduation, issuance of transcript, provisional certificate, degree certificate or cessation of association with the Institute. 13. The Student shall not engage in cheating, plagiarism, contract cheating, proxy attendance, impersonation, unauthorized collaboration, examination misconduct, misuse of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, falsification of records, academic fraud, or any act constituting unfair means under Institute regulations. 9. RESIDENTIAL DISCIPLINE AND HOSTEL CONDUCT The Student acknowledges that all first degree programmes of the Institute are residential programmes and undertakes to comply with all hostel and residential regulations prescribed by the Institute from time to time. The Student shall: (a) reside only in the hostel room allotted by the Institute; (b) not occupy, exchange, sublet, transfer, or permit occupation of any room without authorization; (c) maintain cleanliness, hygiene, discipline, and peaceful coexistence within the hostel premises; (d) observe prescribed quiet hours and refrain from creating noise, nuisance, disturbance, or inconvenience to fellow residents; (e) not organize, host, facilitate, or participate in unauthorized parties, gatherings, celebrations, or activities within hostel premises; (f) not permit unauthorized entry of outsiders, visitors, day scholars, alumni, or off-campus students into hostel premises except in accordance with Institute regulations; (g) not keep or feed any pet, animal, bird, or other living creature within campus or hostel premises; (h) not possess or use prohibited electrical appliances, cooking devices, heating equipment, inflammable materials, hazardous articles, weapons, or prohibited substances within hostel premises; (i) comply with all regulations relating to hostel allotment, vacation stay, summer term accommodation, leave permissions, attendance requirements, and movement restrictions. -- 5 of 11 -- Page 6 of 11 (j) not keep, park, possess, operate, store, or use any motorized vehicle within the campus or hostel premises except as specifically permitted under applicable Institute regulations; provided that bicycles may be used where permitted by the Institute from time to time. PERSONAL BELONGINGS AND LIMITATION OF INSTITUTE LIABILITY The Student shall be solely responsible for the safety, security, custody, and protection of personal belongings, cash, valuables, electronic devices, jewellery, documents, and other personal effects. ANTI-RAGGING, RESPECTFUL CONDUCT AND STUDENT WELFARE The Student shall strictly comply with all Anti-Ragging Regulations, UGC Regulations, judicial directions, and Institute policies. The Student shall not engage in, participate in, encourage, abet, facilitate, conceal, tolerate, or fail to report any act of ragging. The Student shall maintain respectful conduct towards all students, faculty members, employees, visitors, service providers, and stakeholders of the Institute. Physical assault, verbal abuse, intimidation, threats, coercion, bullying, cyberbullying, discrimination, victimization, humiliation, stalking, or conduct adversely affecting the dignity, safety, or well-being of any person shall constitute misconduct. 14. SEXUAL HARASSMENT, GENDER SENSITIVITY AND SAFETY The Student shall comply with the provisions of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, the UGC (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal of Sexual Harassment of Women Employees and Students in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2015, and all applicable Institute policies, procedures, notifications, advisories, and directions issued from time to time relating to gender sensitization, gender equity, safety, dignity, inclusion, prevention of sexual harassment, and respectful conduct. -- 6 of 11 -- Page 7 of 11 The Student shall not engage in sexual harassment, sexual misconduct, gender-based violence, stalking, voyeurism, bullying, cyber harassment, retaliation, victimization, or any unwelcome conduct, whether physical, verbal, written, visual, electronic, or otherwise, that violates the dignity, safety, privacy, or rights of another person or is prohibited under applicable law or Institute regulations. The Student shall cooperate fully with the Internal Committee (IC) / Internal Complaints Committee (ICC), Gender Sensitization Committee, disciplinary authorities, inquiry committees, and other competent authorities of the Institute in relation to any complaint, inquiry, investigation, proceeding, counselling intervention, or preventive measure undertaken by the Institute. The Student shall not directly or indirectly influence, threaten, intimidate, coerce, harass, retaliate against, victimise, or interfere with any complainant, respondent, witness, committee member, investigator, or person associated with any inquiry or proceeding relating to sexual harassment or gender-based misconduct. The Student acknowledges that the Institute may initiate disciplinary proceedings and take appropriate interim, preventive, corrective, or disciplinary measures in accordance with applicable law and Institute regulations, independent of and in addition to any criminal, civil, administrative, or regulatory proceedings. The Student further acknowledges that conduct occurring through electronic means, social media platforms, messaging applications, email communications, video conferencing platforms, anonymous digital accounts, or any other online medium shall be treated on par with physical conduct for the purposes of determining sexual harassment, cyber harassment, stalking, intimidation, or gender-based misconduct. Any violation of this clause may attract action under the Institute's Disciplinary Guidelines, applicable law, and the relevant policies governing prevention and redressal of sexual harassment and gender-based misconduct. 15. ALCOHOL, TOBACCO, SUBSTANCE ABUSE AND PROHIBITED MATERIALS The Institute follows a strict zero-tolerance policy towards alcohol, narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, intoxicants, prohibited chemicals, and substance abuse. The Student shall not consume, possess, procure, store, transport, distribute, finance, facilitate, promote, conceal, or otherwise deal with any prohibited substance under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 ("NDPS Act"), or any other applicable law. Possession of alcohol containers, empty liquor bottles, prohibited paraphernalia, or related materials may be treated as evidence of violation. Any violation occurring within or outside campus premises may attract disciplinary action. Where prohibited substances, narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, alcohol, intoxicants, or other prohibited materials are found within a hostel room, common occupancy space, or area under the control of one or more students, the Institute may, in accordance with its disciplinary procedures, hold all occupants or persons having control over such space jointly or severally responsible unless the facts and circumstances establish otherwise. -- 7 of 11 -- Page 8 of 11 The Student shall cooperate with the Institute and competent authorities in the investigation, prevention, reporting, and deterrence of substance abuse, alcohol-related incidents, violence, cyber misconduct, ragging, sexual misconduct, and other violations and shall not knowingly conceal material information relating thereto. 16. The Institute may communicate with parents, legal guardians, local guardians, hospitals, law enforcement authorities, or competent authorities whenever deemed necessary. 17.
