The Student and Parent/Legal Guardian undertake to pay all applicable fees, dues, charges, penalties, recoveries, and other financial obligations within the timelines prescribed by the Institute and acknowledge that non-payment may attract consequences in accordance with the applicable Institute regulations. -- 3 of 11 -- Page 4 of 11 6. OFF-CAMPUS CONDUCT The disciplinary jurisdiction of the Institute may extend to conduct occurring outside campus premises where such conduct affects the safety, discipline, academic environment, reputation, functioning, or lawful interests of the Institute. This includes conduct during internships, Practice School programmes, industrial visits, exchange programmes, conferences, competitions, festivals, online activities, social events, travel, or any activity where the Student is associated with the Institute. 7. CRIMINAL MISCONDUCT The Student acknowledges that acts constituting offences under applicable laws, including the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, Information Technology Act, 2000, Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 ("NDPS Act"), and other applicable laws may independently constitute misconduct under Institute regulations. The Institute may initiate disciplinary proceedings irrespective of the pendency, compromise, withdrawal, discharge, acquittal, or outcome of any criminal proceeding. 8. ACADEMIC INTEGRITY AND UNFAIR MEANS The Student shall uphold the highest standards of academic honesty and integrity, and ethical conduct, and shall comply with the Institute's Examination Regulations, Academic Integrity Policies, Unfair Means (UFM) Guidelines, Plagiarism Regulations, and other academic regulations, as amended from time to time. The Student shall not engage in cheating, plagiarism, contract cheating, proxy attendance, impersonation, unauthorized collaboration, examination misconduct, misuse of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, falsification of records, academic fraud, or any act constituting unfair means under Institute regulations. 9. DIGITAL CONDUCT, SOCIAL MEDIA, DATA PRIVACY AND CYBER SECURITY The Student shall use digital resources responsibly and shall not: (a) engage in cyberbullying, hacking, phishing, password sharing, malware dissemination, identity theft, unauthorized surveillance, or unauthorized access; (b) publish defamatory, abusive, discriminatory, misleading, threatening, obscene, confidential, or reputation-damaging content; (c) unlawfully collect, process, store, disclose, transmit, or misuse personal data, recordings, photographs, videos, academic records, health information, identity documents, or confidential information; (d) engage in unauthorized photography, videography, audio recording, live streaming, or dissemination of recordings from classrooms, hostels, offices, laboratories, examinations, disciplinary proceedings, medical facilities, or private spaces. 10. RESIDENTIAL DISCIPLINE AND HOSTEL CONDUCT -- 4 of 11 -- Page 5 of 11 The Student acknowledges that all first degree programmes of the Institute are residential programmes and undertakes to comply with all hostel and residential regulations prescribed by the Institute from time to time. The Student shall: (a) reside only in the hostel room allotted by the Institute; (b) not occupy, exchange, sublet, transfer, or permit occupation of any room without authorization; (c) maintain cleanliness, hygiene, discipline, and peaceful coexistence within the hostel premises; (d) observe prescribed quiet hours and refrain from creating noise, nuisance, disturbance, or inconvenience to fellow residents; (e) not organize, host, facilitate, or participate in unauthorized parties, gatherings, celebrations, or activities within hostel premises; (f) not permit unauthorized entry of outsiders, visitors, day scholars, alumni, or off- campus students into hostel premises except in accordance with Institute regulations; (g) not keep or feed any pet, animal, bird, or other living creature within campus or hostel premises; (h) not possess or use prohibited electrical appliances, cooking devices, heating equipment, inflammable materials, hazardous articles, weapons, or prohibited substances within hostel premises; (i) comply with all regulations relating to hostel allotment, vacation stay, summer term accommodation, leave permissions, attendance requirements, and movement restrictions. (j) not keep, park, possess, operate, store, or use any motorized vehicle within the campus or hostel premises except as specifically permitted under applicable Institute regulations; provided that bicycles may be used where permitted by the Institute from time to time. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Institute reserves the right, in its sole discretion and in accordance with applicable regulations, to deny, suspend, withdraw, modify, or restrict hostel accommodation or residential privileges on grounds relating to safety, security, health, mental well-being, discipline, welfare, administrative requirements, or any other legitimate institutional consideration. 11. PERSONAL BELONGINGS AND LIMITATION OF INSTITUTE LIABILITY The Student shall be solely responsible for the safety, security, custody, and protection of personal belongings, cash, valuables, electronic devices, jewellery, documents, and other personal effects. The Institute shall not be responsible for any loss, theft, damage, destruction, or misplacement thereof except to the extent required under applicable law. 12. UNAUTHORIZED COMMERCIAL ACTIVITIES AND MULTI-LEVEL MARKETING -- 5 of 11 -- Page 6 of 11 The Student shall not engage in, promote, facilitate, solicit, market, recruit for, or conduct any multi-level marketing, pyramid scheme, unauthorized commercial activity, direct selling activity, or business solicitation within campus or hostel premises without prior written approval of the Institute. 13. ANTI-RAGGING, RESPECTFUL CONDUCT AND STUDENT WELFARE The Student shall strictly comply with all Anti-Ragging Regulations, UGC Regulations, judicial directions, and Institute policies. The Student shall not engage in, participate in, encourage, abet, facilitate, conceal, tolerate, or fail to report any act of ragging. The Student shall maintain respectful conduct towards all students, faculty members, employees, visitors, service providers, and stakeholders of the Institute. Physical assault, verbal abuse, intimidation, threats, coercion, bullying, cyberbullying, discrimination, victimization, humiliation, stalking, or conduct adversely affecting the dignity, safety, or well-being of any person shall constitute misconduct. 14. SEXUAL HARASSMENT, GENDER SENSITIVITY AND SAFETY The Student shall comply with the provisions of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, the UGC (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal of Sexual Harassment of Women Employees and Students in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2015, and all applicable Institute policies, procedures, notifications, advisories, and directions issued from time to time relating to gender sensitization, gender equity, safety, dignity, inclusion, prevention of sexual harassment, and respectful conduct. The Student shall not engage in sexual harassment, sexual misconduct, gender-based violence, stalking, voyeurism, bullying, cyber harassment, retaliation, victimization, or any unwelcome conduct, whether physical, verbal, written, visual, electronic, or otherwise, that violates the dignity, safety, privacy, or rights of another person or is prohibited under applicable law or Institute regulations. The Student shall cooperate fully with the Internal Committee (IC) / Internal Complaints Committee (ICC), Gender Sensitization Committee, disciplinary authorities, inquiry committees, and other competent authorities of the Institute in relation to any complaint, inquiry, investigation, proceeding, counselling intervention, or preventive measure undertaken by the Institute. The Student shall not directly or indirectly influence, threaten, intimidate, coerce, harass, retaliate against, victimise, or interfere with any complainant, respondent, witness, committee member, investigator, or person associated with any inquiry or proceeding relating to sexual harassment or gender-based misconduct. The Student acknowledges that the Institute may initiate disciplinary proceedings and take appropriate interim, preventive, corrective, or disciplinary measures in accordance with applicable law and Institute regulations, independent of and in addition to any criminal, civil, administrative, or regulatory proceedings. -- 6 of 11 -- Page 7 of 11 The Student further acknowledges that conduct occurring through electronic means, social media platforms, messaging applications, email communications, video conferencing platforms, anonymous digital accounts, or any other online medium shall be treated on par with physical conduct for the purposes of determining sexual harassment, cyber harassment, stalking, intimidation, or gender-based misconduct. Any violation of this clause may attract action under the Institute's Disciplinary Guidelines, applicable law, and the relevant policies governing prevention and redressal of sexual harassment and gender-based misconduct. 15. ALCOHOL, TOBACCO, SUBSTANCE ABUSE AND PROHIBITED MATERIALS The Institute follows a strict zero-tolerance policy towards alcohol, narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, intoxicants, prohibited chemicals, and substance abuse. The Student shall not consume, possess, procure, store, transport, distribute, finance, facilitate, promote, conceal, or otherwise deal with any prohibited substance under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 ("NDPS Act"), or any other applicable law. Possession of alcohol containers, empty liquor bottles, prohibited paraphernalia, or related materials may be treated as evidence of violation. Any violation occurring within or outside campus premises may attract disciplinary action. Where prohibited substances, narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, alcohol, intoxicants, or other prohibited materials are found within a hostel room, common occupancy space, or area under the control of one or more students, the Institute may, in accordance with its disciplinary procedures, hold all occupants or persons having control over such space jointly or severally responsible unless the facts and circumstances establish otherwise. The Student shall cooperate with the Institute and competent authorities in the investigation, prevention, reporting, and deterrence of substance abuse, alcohol-related incidents, violence, cyber misconduct, ragging, sexual misconduct, and other violations and shall not knowingly conceal material information relating thereto. 16. MEDICAL EMERGENCIES, TESTING AND WELFARE INTERVENTIONS Subject to applicable law and medical protocols, the Student and Parent/Legal Guardian consent to medical examination, testing, assessment, emergency treatment, hospitalization, counselling, psychological intervention, welfare intervention, and other appropriate measures where reasonably required in the interests of safety, health, welfare, investigation of substance abuse, intoxication, self-harm risk, violent conduct, or other serious incidents. The Institute may communicate with parents, legal guardians, local guardians, hospitals, law enforcement authorities, or competent authorities whenever deemed necessary. 17. PRE-EXISTING MEDICAL CONDITIONS AND WELFARE DISCLOSURES: The Student and Parent/Legal Guardian undertake to disclose, to the best of their knowledge, any significant pre-existing medical condition, chronic illness, psychological condition, mental health concern, disability, allergy, medication dependency, or any circumstance requiring -- 7 of 11 -- Page 8 of 11 special care, support, accommodation, or emergency intervention that may reasonably affect the Student's health, safety, welfare, or residential life at the Institute. The Student and Parent/Legal Guardian further undertake to promptly inform the Institute of any material change in such condition during the period of enrolment. 18. EVENTS, FESTIVALS, STUDENT ACTIVITIES AND REPRESENTATION OF THE INSTITUTE The Student shall comply with all directions issued by the Institute during Student Union Events, conferences, competitions, student activities, club events, outreach programmes, Practice School programmes, internships, exchange programmes, industrial visits, and all other activities conducted, sponsored, recognized, or attended under the name of the Institute. Misconduct during such activities shall be treated as misconduct under Institute regulations irrespective of whether such activity occurs within or outside campus premises. 19. FALSE COMPLAINTS, EVIDENCE TAMPERING AND OBSTRUCTION OF PROCEEDINGS The Student shall not: (a) submit knowingly false complaints; (b) fabricate, alter, suppress, conceal, or destroy evidence; (c) intimidate witnesses; (d) influence complainants, respondents, witnesses, investigators, or disciplinary authorities; (e) obstruct, interfere with, or undermine investigations, inquiries, disciplinary proceedings, grievance proceedings, or institutional processes. Any such conduct shall constitute serious misconduct. 20. SEARCH, INSPECTION AND CONFISCATION Subject to applicable law and Institute procedures, authorized Institute officials may inspect hostel rooms, lockers, bags, vehicles, electronic devices, storage spaces, or other belongings where reasonable grounds exist relating to safety, security, prohibited articles, misconduct, or protection of Institute interests. Unauthorized, unlawful, prohibited, dangerous, or objectionable materials may be confiscated and dealt with in accordance with applicable law and Institute regulations. 21. DISCIPLINARY AUTHORITY OF THE INSTITUTE The Student acknowledges the authority of the Institute to investigate, inquire into, and adjudicate violations of Institute regulations. The Student further acknowledges that any violation may attract one or more sanctions prescribed under the Institute's Disciplinary Guidelines, as amended from time to time. -- 8 of 11 -- Page 9 of 11 Such sanctions may be imposed independently or in addition to any civil, criminal, regulatory, academic, administrative, or financial consequences. 22. PARENT / LEGAL GUARDIAN RESPONSIBILITIES The Parent / Legal Guardian undertakes: (a) to cooperate fully with the Institute in academic, disciplinary, welfare, counselling, administrative, legal, and safety matters concerning the Student; (b) to promptly respond to communications issued by the Institute; (c) to encourage compliance with Institute regulations; (d) to provide updated contact information at all times; (e) to assist the Institute in addressing serious welfare, disciplinary, medical, or safety concerns involving the Student. 23. CONTINUING DUTY OF DISCLOSURE The Student shall promptly disclose to the Institute any fact, circumstance, investigation, disciplinary proceeding, criminal proceeding, regulatory action, or information that may materially affect the Student's eligibility, enrolment, academic standing, residential status, or continued association with the Institute. Failure to disclose such information may constitute misconduct. 24. EMERGENCY POWERS OF THE INSTITUTE In situations involving safety, health, security, welfare, missing students, criminal allegations, accidents, disasters, public emergencies, or other urgent circumstances, the Institute may take such immediate measures as it reasonably considers necessary in the interests of safety, security, discipline, and welfare. 25. TRAVEL, TRANSPORTATION AND OFF-CAMPUS ACTIVITIES The Student acknowledges that travel, riding, driving, commuting, excursions, personal visits, private trips, outings, and activities undertaken outside campus premises are ordinarily at the Student's own risk and responsibility. The Institute shall not be liable for any accident, injury, illness, loss of life, loss of property, theft, damage, criminal act, or any other unforeseen event occurring outside the scope of its control, supervision, authorization, or responsibility, except to the extent required under applicable law. The Student shall comply with all applicable laws relating to transportation, road safety, licensing requirements, and public safety while undertaking any off-campus activity. 26. NO WAIVER Any delay, omission, forbearance, or failure by the Institute to exercise any right, power, authority, or remedy shall not constitute a waiver thereof. -- 9 of 11 -- Page 10 of 11 27. SEVERABILITY If any provision of this Undertaking is held invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. 28. JURISDICTION This Undertaking shall be governed by the laws of India. Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Undertaking shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the competent courts having territorial jurisdiction over the concerned campus of BITS Pilani. -- 10 of 11 -- Page 11 of 11 ATTESTATION AND DECLARATION We hereby certify, declare, and confirm that: (a) we have carefully read each page & every points of this Undertaking; (b) we have fully understood the contents, implications, obligations, liabilities, disciplinary consequences, and responsibilities arising hereunder; (c) we have been afforded adequate opportunity to seek clarification regarding any provision of this Undertaking; (d) we are executing this Undertaking voluntarily, consciously, and without coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, mistake, or misunderstanding; (e) all information furnished by us is true, complete, and accurate; (f) we acknowledge and accept the Institute's zero-tolerance approach towards ragging, substance abuse, sexual misconduct, violence, cyber misconduct, academic dishonesty, admission fraud, misuse of personal data, and other serious violations; (g) we agree to remain bound by all present and future Institute regulations, policies, guidelines, notifications, circulars, and lawful directions issued from time to time. We understand that admission to the Institute, continued enrolment, campus living participation in academic and co-curricular activities, use of Institute facilities, and allotment of hostel accommodation are subject to compliance with the provisions of this Undertaking and all applicable Institute regulations. -- 1 of 11 -- Page 2 of 11 2. COMPLIANCE WITH INSTITUTE POLICIES The Student shall comply with and remain bound by all Statutes, Ordinances, Regulations, Rules, Codes, Policies, Handbooks, Guidelines, Circulars, Notifications, Advisories, Standard Operating Procedures, and lawful directions issued by the Institute from time to time, including but not limited to: (a) Student Code of Conduct: (i) Hostel Rules and Residential Regulations (Available on SWD portal, as amended time to time); (ii) Institute Disciplinary Guidelines and all sanctions prescribed therein (Available on the SWD portal, as amended time to time); (b) Anti-Ragging Regulations and related policies; (c) Prevention of Sexual Harassment Policies and Internal Committee procedures; (d) Examination Regulations, Academic Integrity Policies, Unfair Means Guidelines, and Plagiarism Regulations; (e) Information Technology Policies, Artificial Intelligence Usage Policies, Cyber Security Policies, and Network Usage Policies; (f) Data Privacy Policies and Personal Data Protection Guidelines issued under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023; (g) Social Media Policy, Brand Usage Guidelines, and Media Interaction Guidelines; (h) Practice School Regulations, Internship Regulations, Student Activity Centre Rules, Club and Association Rules; (i) Student Union’s Cultural, Technical, Sports, and other student event regulations; (j) Health, Safety, Security, Emergency Response, and Welfare Policies; (k) Any future amendment, modification, replacement, revision, or re-enactment of any of the foregoing policies, regulations, rules, guidelines, or provisions shall be deemed to form an integral part of this undertaking and shall be binding upon the undersigned. 3. ADMISSION VALIDITY AND ELIGIBILITY The Student and Parent/Legal Guardian declare that all information, records, documents, certificates, declarations, and credentials furnished to the Institute are true, complete, genuine, authentic, and accurate. The Student and Parent/Legal Guardian further undertake and agree to abide by the following: -- 2 of 11 -- Page 3 of 11 (a) No forged, fabricated, altered, manipulated, false, misleading, or fraudulently obtained document has been submitted; (b) No material fact relating to eligibility, academic qualifications, identity, conduct, disciplinary history, category, nationality, or admission has been concealed; (c) Admission has not been secured through impersonation, fraud, misrepresentation, collusion, suppression of facts, or any unlawful means; (d) The Student has not used any unfair means, proxy candidate, impersonation, technological manipulation, organized malpractice, or any prohibited practice in any admission-related process. The Institute shall have the right to verify or re-verify any information at any stage during or after the Student's academic association with the Institute. If at any stage it is found, determined, or reasonably established after due verification that admission was obtained by fraud, impersonation, forged documents, false declarations, suppression of material facts or any admission-related process, the Institute may, without prejudice to any other remedy available under law: (i) cancel admission; (ii) withdraw registration; (iii) cancel hostel allotment; (iv) suspend or expel the Student; (v) cancel examination results; (vi) revoke scholarships, awards, medals, distinctions, credits, degrees, diplomas, certificates, or academic benefits; (vii) initiate disciplinary, civil, criminal, or regulatory proceedings. 4. CONDUCT BECOMING OF A STUDENT OF BITS PILANI The Student shall at all times conduct himself/herself in a manner consistent with the dignity, values, reputation, discipline, and standards expected from a student of BITS Pilani. The Student shall not engage in gambling, betting, wagering, online gaming for monetary stakes, speculative gaming, poker, card gambling, fantasy gaming involving monetary consideration, or any similar activity prohibited by law or Institute regulations. Any conduct which adversely affects or is reasonably likely to adversely affect the reputation, goodwill, academic standing, functioning, safety, discipline, or lawful interests of the Institute may constitute misconduct. -- 3 of 11 -- Page 4 of 11 5. FEES, CHARGES AND FINANCIAL OBLIGATIONS The Student and Parent/Legal Guardian acknowledge that they have carefully reviewed and understood the fee structure applicable to the Programme, including tuition fees, hostel and mess charges, Practice School fees, summer term fees, laboratory charges, caution deposits, examination-related charges, and any other fees or charges prescribed by the Institute from time to time. The Student and Parent/Legal Guardian undertake to pay all applicable fees, dues, charges, penalties, recoveries, and other financial obligations within the timelines prescribed by the Institute and acknowledge that non-payment may attract consequences in accordance with the applicable Institute regulations. 6. OFF-CAMPUS CONDUCT The disciplinary jurisdiction of the Institute may extend to conduct occurring outside campus premises where such conduct affects the safety, discipline, academic environment, reputation, functioning, or lawful interests of the Institute. This includes conduct during internships, Practice School programmes, industrial visits, exchange programmes, conferences, competitions, festivals, online activities, social events, travel, or any activity where the Student is associated with the Institute. 7. CRIMINAL MISCONDUCT The Student acknowledges that acts constituting offences under applicable laws, including the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, Information Technology Act, 2000, Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 ("NDPS Act"), and other applicable laws may independently constitute misconduct under Institute regulations. The Institute may initiate disciplinary proceedings irrespective of the pendency, compromise, withdrawal, discharge, acquittal, or outcome of any criminal proceeding. 8. ACADEMIC INTEGRITY AND UNFAIR MEANS The Student shall uphold the highest standards of academic honesty and integrity, and ethical conduct, and shall comply with the Institute's Examination Regulations, Academic Integrity Policies, Unfair Means (UFM) Guidelines, Plagiarism Regulations, and other academic regulations, as amended from time to time. The Student shall not engage in cheating, plagiarism, contract cheating, proxy attendance, impersonation, unauthorized collaboration, examination misconduct, misuse of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools, falsification of records, academic fraud, or any act constituting unfair means under Institute regulations. 9. DIGITAL CONDUCT, SOCIAL MEDIA, DATA PRIVACY AND CYBER SECURITY The Student shall use digital resources responsibly and shall not: -- 4 of 11 -- Page 5 of 11 (a) engage in cyberbullying, hacking, phishing, password sharing, malware dissemination, identity theft, unauthorized surveillance, or unauthorized access; (b) publish defamatory, abusive, discriminatory, misleading, threatening, obscene, confidential, or reputation-damaging content; (c) unlawfully collect, process, store, disclose, transmit, or misuse personal data, recordings, photographs, videos, academic records, health information, identity documents, or confidential information; (d) engage in unauthorized photography, videography, audio recording, live streaming, or dissemination of recordings from classrooms, hostels, offices, laboratories, examinations, disciplinary proceedings, medical facilities, or private spaces. 10. RESIDENTIAL DISCIPLINE AND HOSTEL CONDUCT The Student acknowledges that all first degree programmes of the Institute are residential programmes and undertakes to comply with all hostel and residential regulations prescribed by the Institute from time to time. The Student shall: (a) reside only in the hostel room allotted by the Institute; (b) not occupy, exchange, sublet, transfer, or permit occupation of any room without authorization; (c) maintain cleanliness, hygiene, discipline, and peaceful coexistence within the hostel premises; (d) observe prescribed quiet hours and refrain from creating noise, nuisance, disturbance, or inconvenience to fellow residents; (e) not organize, host, facilitate, or participate in unauthorized parties, gatherings, celebrations, or activities within hostel premises; (f) not permit unauthorized entry of outsiders, visitors, day scholars, alumni, or off-campus students into hostel premises except in accordance with Institute regulations; (g) not keep or feed any pet, animal, bird, or other living creature within campus or hostel premises; (h) not possess or use prohibited electrical appliances, cooking devices, heating equipment, inflammable materials, hazardous articles, weapons, or prohibited substances within hostel premises; (i) comply with all regulations relating to hostel allotment, vacation stay, summer term accommodation, leave permissions, attendance requirements, and movement restrictions. -- 5 of 11 -- Page 6 of 11 (j) not keep, park, possess, operate, store, or use any motorized vehicle within the campus or hostel premises except as specifically permitted under applicable Institute regulations; provided that bicycles may be used where permitted by the Institute from time to time. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Institute reserves the right, in its sole discretion and in accordance with applicable regulations, to deny, suspend, withdraw, modify, or restrict hostel accommodation or residential privileges on grounds relating to safety, security, health, mental well-being, discipline, welfare, administrative requirements, or any other legitimate institutional consideration. 11. PERSONAL BELONGINGS AND LIMITATION OF INSTITUTE LIABILITY The Student shall be solely responsible for the safety, security, custody, and protection of personal belongings, cash, valuables, electronic devices, jewellery, documents, and other personal effects. The Institute shall not be responsible for any loss, theft, damage, destruction, or misplacement thereof except to the extent required under applicable law. 12. UNAUTHORIZED COMMERCIAL ACTIVITIES AND MULTI-LEVEL MARKETING The Student shall not engage in, promote, facilitate, solicit, market, recruit for, or conduct any multi-level marketing, pyramid scheme, unauthorized commercial activity, direct selling activity, or business solicitation within campus or hostel premises without prior written approval of the Institute. 13. ANTI-RAGGING, RESPECTFUL CONDUCT AND STUDENT WELFARE The Student shall strictly comply with all Anti-Ragging Regulations, UGC Regulations, judicial directions, and Institute policies. The Student shall not engage in, participate in, encourage, abet, facilitate, conceal, tolerate, or fail to report any act of ragging. The Student shall maintain respectful conduct towards all students, faculty members, employees, visitors, service providers, and stakeholders of the Institute. Physical assault, verbal abuse, intimidation, threats, coercion, bullying, cyberbullying, discrimination, victimization, humiliation, stalking, or conduct adversely affecting the dignity, safety, or well-being of any person shall constitute misconduct. 14. SEXUAL HARASSMENT, GENDER SENSITIVITY AND SAFETY The Student shall comply with the provisions of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, the UGC (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal of Sexual Harassment of Women Employees and Students in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2015, and all applicable Institute policies, procedures, notifications, advisories, and directions issued from time to time relating to gender sensitization, gender equity, safety, dignity, inclusion, prevention of sexual harassment, and respectful conduct. -- 6 of 11 -- Page 7 of 11 The Student shall not engage in sexual harassment, sexual misconduct, gender-based violence, stalking, voyeurism, bullying, cyber harassment, retaliation, victimization, or any unwelcome conduct, whether physical, verbal, written, visual, electronic, or otherwise, that violates the dignity, safety, privacy, or rights of another person or is prohibited under applicable law or Institute regulations. The Student shall cooperate fully with the Internal Committee (IC) / Internal Complaints Committee (ICC), Gender Sensitization Committee, disciplinary authorities, inquiry committees, and other competent authorities of the Institute in relation to any complaint, inquiry, investigation, proceeding, counselling intervention, or preventive measure undertaken by the Institute. The Student shall not directly or indirectly influence, threaten, intimidate, coerce, harass, retaliate against, victimise, or interfere with any complainant, respondent, witness, committee member, investigator, or person associated with any inquiry or proceeding relating to sexual harassment or gender-based misconduct. The Student acknowledges that the Institute may initiate disciplinary proceedings and take appropriate interim, preventive, corrective, or disciplinary measures in accordance with applicable law and Institute regulations, independent of and in addition to any criminal, civil, administrative, or regulatory proceedings. The Student further acknowledges that conduct occurring through electronic means, social media platforms, messaging applications, email communications, video conferencing platforms, anonymous digital accounts, or any other online medium shall be treated on par with physical conduct for the purposes of determining sexual harassment, cyber harassment, stalking, intimidation, or gender-based misconduct. Any violation of this clause may attract action under the Institute's Disciplinary Guidelines, applicable law, and the relevant policies governing prevention and redressal of sexual harassment and gender-based misconduct. 15. ALCOHOL, TOBACCO, SUBSTANCE ABUSE AND PROHIBITED MATERIALS The Institute follows a strict zero-tolerance policy towards alcohol, narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, intoxicants, prohibited chemicals, and substance abuse. The Student shall not consume, possess, procure, store, transport, distribute, finance, facilitate, promote, conceal, or otherwise deal with any prohibited substance under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 ("NDPS Act"), or any other applicable law. Possession of alcohol containers, empty liquor bottles, prohibited paraphernalia, or related materials may be treated as evidence of violation. Any violation occurring within or outside campus premises may attract disciplinary action. Where prohibited substances, narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, alcohol, intoxicants, or other prohibited materials are found within a hostel room, common occupancy space, or area under the control of one or more students, the Institute may, in accordance with its disciplinary procedures, hold all occupants or persons having control over such space jointly or severally responsible unless the facts and circumstances establish otherwise. -- 7 of 11 -- Page 8 of 11 The Student shall cooperate with the Institute and competent authorities in the investigation, prevention, reporting, and deterrence of substance abuse, alcohol-related incidents, violence, cyber misconduct, ragging, sexual misconduct, and other violations and shall not knowingly conceal material information relating thereto. 16. MEDICAL EMERGENCIES, TESTING AND WELFARE INTERVENTIONS Subject to applicable law and medical protocols, the Student and Parent/Legal Guardian consent to medical examination, testing, assessment, emergency treatment, hospitalization, counselling, psychological intervention, welfare intervention, and other appropriate measures where reasonably required in the interests of safety, health, welfare, investigation of substance abuse, intoxication, self-harm risk, violent conduct, or other serious incidents. The Institute may communicate with parents, legal guardians, local guardians, hospitals, law enforcement authorities, or competent authorities whenever deemed necessary. 17. PRE-EXISTING MEDICAL CONDITIONS AND WELFARE DISCLOSURES: The Student and Parent/Legal Guardian undertake to disclose, to the best of their knowledge, any significant pre-existing medical condition, chronic illness, psychological condition, mental health concern, disability, allergy, medication dependency, or any circumstance requiring special care, support, accommodation, or emergency intervention that may reasonably affect the Student's health, safety, welfare, or residential life at the Institute. The Student and Parent/Legal Guardian further undertake to promptly inform the Institute of any material change in such condition during the period of enrolment. 18. EVENTS, FESTIVALS, STUDENT ACTIVITIES AND REPRESENTATION OF THE INSTITUTE The Student shall comply with all directions issued by the Institute during Student Union Events, conferences, competitions, student activities, club events, outreach programmes, Practice School programmes, internships, exchange programmes, industrial visits, and all other activities conducted, sponsored, recognized, or attended under the name of the Institute. Misconduct during such activities shall be treated as misconduct under Institute regulations irrespective of whether such activity occurs within or outside campus premises. 19. FALSE COMPLAINTS, EVIDENCE TAMPERING AND OBSTRUCTION OF PROCEEDINGS The Student shall not: (a) submit knowingly false complaints; (b) fabricate, alter, suppress, conceal, or destroy evidence; (c) intimidate witnesses; -- 8 of 11 -- Page 9 of 11 (d) influence complainants, respondents, witnesses, investigators, or disciplinary authorities; (e) obstruct, interfere with, or undermine investigations, inquiries, disciplinary proceedings, grievance proceedings, or institutional processes. Any such conduct shall constitute serious misconduct. 20. SEARCH, INSPECTION AND CONFISCATION Subject to applicable law and Institute procedures, authorized Institute officials may inspect hostel rooms, lockers, bags, vehicles, electronic devices, storage spaces, or other belongings where reasonable grounds exist relating to safety, security, prohibited articles, misconduct, or protection of Institute interests. Unauthorized, unlawful, prohibited, dangerous, or objectionable materials may be confiscated and dealt with in accordance with applicable law and Institute regulations. 21. DISCIPLINARY AUTHORITY OF THE INSTITUTE The Student acknowledges the authority of the Institute to investigate, inquire into, and adjudicate violations of Institute regulations. The Student further acknowledges that any violation may attract one or more sanctions prescribed under the Institute's Disciplinary Guidelines, as amended from time to time. Such sanctions may be imposed independently or in addition to any civil, criminal, regulatory, academic, administrative, or financial consequences. 22. PARENT / LEGAL GUARDIAN RESPONSIBILITIES The Parent / Legal Guardian undertakes: (a) to cooperate fully with the Institute in academic, disciplinary, welfare, counselling, administrative, legal, and safety matters concerning the Student; (b) to promptly respond to communications issued by the Institute; (c) to encourage compliance with Institute regulations; (d) to provide updated contact information at all times; (e) to assist the Institute in addressing serious welfare, disciplinary, medical, or safety concerns involving the Student. 23. CONTINUING DUTY OF DISCLOSURE The Student shall promptly disclose to the Institute any fact, circumstance, investigation, disciplinary proceeding, criminal proceeding, regulatory action, or information that may materially -- 9 of 11 -- Page 10 of 11 affect the Student's eligibility, enrolment, academic standing, residential status, or continued association with the Institute. Failure to disclose such information may constitute misconduct. 24. EMERGENCY POWERS OF THE INSTITUTE In situations involving safety, health, security, welfare, missing students, criminal allegations, accidents, disasters, public emergencies, or other urgent circumstances, the Institute may take such immediate measures as it reasonably considers necessary in the interests of safety, security, discipline, and welfare. 25. TRAVEL, TRANSPORTATION AND OFF-CAMPUS ACTIVITIES The Student acknowledges that travel, riding, driving, commuting, excursions, personal visits, private trips, outings, and activities undertaken outside campus premises are ordinarily at the Student's own risk and responsibility. The Institute shall not be liable for any accident, injury, illness, loss of life, loss of property, theft, damage, criminal act, or any other unforeseen event occurring outside the scope of its control, supervision, authorization, or responsibility, except to the extent required under applicable law. The Student shall comply with all applicable laws relating to transportation, road safety, licensing requirements, and public safety while undertaking any off-campus activity. 26. NO WAIVER Any delay, omission, forbearance, or failure by the Institute to exercise any right, power, authority, or remedy shall not constitute a waiver thereof. 27. SEVERABILITY If any provision of this Undertaking is held invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. 28. JURISDICTION This Undertaking shall be governed by the laws of India. Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Undertaking shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the competent courts having territorial jurisdiction over the concerned campus of BITS Pilani. -- 10 of 11 -- Page 11 of 11 ATTESTATION AND DECLARATION We hereby certify, declare, and confirm that: (a) we have carefully read each page & every points of this Undertaking; (b) we have fully understood the contents, implications, obligations, liabilities, disciplinary consequences, and responsibilities arising hereunder; (c) we have been afforded adequate opportunity to seek clarification regarding any provision of this Undertaking; (d) we are executing this Undertaking voluntarily, consciously, and without coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, mistake, or misunderstanding; (e) all information furnished by us is true, complete, and accurate; (f) we acknowledge and accept the Institute's zero-tolerance approach towards ragging, substance abuse, sexual misconduct, violence, cyber misconduct, academic dishonesty, admission fraud, misuse of personal data, and other serious violations; (g) we agree to remain bound by all present and future Institute regulations, policies, guidelines, notifications, circulars, and lawful directions issued from time to time. 1 AFFIDAVIT-CUM-DECLARATION AND INDEMNITY BOND (For Scholarship / Fee Waiver / Financial Assistance) (To be executed on a ₹100/- Non-Judicial Stamp Paper and duly notarized, if you have been selected for upfront Merit-cum-Need Scholarship or Tuition Blind scheme) I, Mr./Ms. ____________________________, S/o/D/o ____________________________, BITSAT-2026 Application No. ____________________, having been offered admission to BITS-UB 2+2 International Collaborative Programme at Birla Institute of Technology and Science, Pilani ("BITS Pilani" / "Institute")_______Campus, together with my Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s), namely: 1. Mr./Mrs. ____________________________ 2. Mr./Mrs. ____________________________ do hereby solemnly affirm, declare and undertake as follows: 1. I/We have applied for scholarship, fee waiver, financial assistance, concession or other financial benefit offered by the Institute ("Scholarship") and understand that grant of such benefit is subject to fulfillment of the eligibility criteria prescribed by the Institute from time to time. -- 1 of 3 -- 2 2. For the purpose of Scholarship eligibility, "Family Income" shall mean the aggregate gross annual income of the Student's Father and Mother from all sources. Where eligibility is based on a Legal Guardian, it shall mean the aggregate gross annual income of such Legal Guardian(s). 3. I/We declare that all information, declarations, Income Tax Returns, income certificates, salary records, financial statements and other documents submitted to the Institute in support of the Scholarship application are true, complete, genuine and accurate. 4. I/We specifically declare that the Income Tax Returns for Assessment Year(s) 2025-26 and all supporting financial documents submitted to the Institute are authentic, validly issued and have not been forged, fabricated, manipulated, altered, procured by misrepresentation or otherwise unlawfully obtained. 5. I/We further declare that all sources of income of the Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s), including salary, business income, professional income, consultancy income, rental income, agricultural income, investment income, pension, foreign income and any other income whatsoever, have been fully and truthfully disclosed to the Institute and that no material financial information has been concealed, omitted or suppressed. 6. I/We acknowledge and undertake that the Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s) whose names appear in the income documents submitted at the time of admission shall continue to form the basis for determining the Student's eligibility for scholarship throughout the Student's tenure at the Institute. The Student shall, however, be required to submit the latest income documents of the same Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s) at the beginning of each semester to the Student Welfare Division of the respective campus for assessment of the Student's scholarship eligibility. The Institute shall not permit the substitution or replacement of such Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s) with any other person for the purpose of determining the Student's scholarship eligibility. 7. I/We acknowledge and agree that Scholarship eligibility shall be reviewed by the Institute from time to time in accordance with the applicable Scholarship policy. I/We undertake to submit, at my/our own responsibility, the prescribed Income Tax Returns, income certificates, declarations and such other financial documents as may be required by the Institute for each academic year or at such intervals as may be prescribed by the Institute. Failure to submit the required documents within the prescribed timeline may result in withholding, discontinuance or withdrawal of the Scholarship and, if any Scholarship amount or financial benefit has already been granted on a provisional basis, the same shall be liable to be recovered by the Institute. 8. I/We acknowledge and agree that grant, continuation, renewal, enhancement, reduction, suspension or withdrawal of any Scholarship, fee waiver, financial assistance, concession or other financial benefit shall be solely at the discretion of the Institute and subject to the applicable rules, policies, eligibility criteria and conditions prescribed by the Institute from time to time. I/We further confirm that I/we have read and understood the applicable Scholarship terms and conditions and that no Scholarship or financial assistance shall be claimed as a matter of right. The Institute shall be entitled to discontinue or withdraw the Scholarship upon the Student ceasing to satisfy any prescribed eligibility condition or upon occurrence of any event under the applicable rules or policies of the Institute including, without limitation, disciplinary action, misconduct, submission of incorrect information, failure to submit prescribed documents, or failure to satisfy the applicable financial or minimum academic eligibility criteria. 9. I/We expressly authorize the Institute, at any stage before admission, during the programme, after graduation, after issuance of any academic credential, or at any subsequent time, to verify or cause verification of any declaration, Income Tax Return, certificate, financial document or supporting record submitted in connection with the Scholarship application from any authority, employer, institution, bank, financial institution or other source considered appropriate by the Institute. 10. If at any stage it is found that any declaration, Income Tax Return, certificate or supporting document is false, forged, fabricated, misleading, incomplete, manipulated, or that any material income or financial -- 2 of 3 -- 3 information has been concealed or suppressed, or that the Student was otherwise not eligible for the Scholarship, the Institute shall be entitled to withdraw or cancel the Scholarship, recover the entire financial benefit granted, demand payment of the applicable fees and charges, and initiate such disciplinary, civil, criminal or other proceedings as may be permissible under applicable law and the rules, policies and regulations of the Institute.The aforesaid rights of the Institute may be exercised irrespective of whether such discrepancy, concealment, misrepresentation or ineligibility is discovered before admission, during the course of study, after graduation, or after issuance of any academic credential. 11. I/We jointly and severally agree to indemnify and keep indemnified BITS Pilani, its campuses, officers, employees and representatives against all losses, claims, liabilities, damages, costs and expenses arising out of any false declaration, forged document, concealment of income, misrepresentation or wrongful receipt of Scholarship benefits. 12. I/We agree that any amount determined by the Institute to be recoverable under this Affidavit-cum- Declaration and Indemnity Bond shall constitute a lawful debt due to the Institute and shall remain recoverable notwithstanding completion of studies, withdrawal from the programme, graduation, issuance of transcript, provisional certificate, degree certificate or cessation of association with the Institute. 13. The Student and Parent(s)/Legal Guardian(s) shall be jointly and severally liable for all obligations arising under this Affidavit-cum-Declaration and Indemnity Bond, which shall remain valid and binding until all obligations hereunder have been fully discharged. 14. This Affidavit-cum-Declaration and Indemnity Bond shall be governed by the laws of India and shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the competent courts at Jhunjhunu/Pilani, Rajasthan. VERIFICATION I/We hereby verify that the contents of this Affidavit-cum-Declaration and Indemnity Bond are true and correct to the best of our knowledge and belief and that nothing material has been concealed therefrom. Eligibility A student who satisfies all of the following criteria is eligible to apply to Integrated First Degree programmes through International Students Admissions’ scheme: • Only citizens (candidates holding foreign passports) of a country other than India can apply. • For admission to all the integrated First Degree programmes, candidates should have passed the 12th grade examination of the 10+2 system from a recognized board or its equivalent with adequate proficiency in English. Except for admission to B.Pharm. and B.E. Environmental and Sustainability Engineering with PCB input, the candidates should have Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects along with one of Chemistry/Biotechnology/Biology/Technical Vocational Subjects. • For admission to B.Pharm. and B.E. Environmental and Sustainability Engineering (with PCB input) programmes, candidates should have Physics, & Biology/Mathematics as compulsory subjects along with one of Chemistry/Biotechnology/Technical Vocational Subjects. • In addition, the candidate under ISA scheme should have obtained a minimum aggregate of 75% marks in Physics, Mathematics, & Chemistry/Biology/Biotechnology/Technical Vocational subjects with at least 60% marks in each of these subjects in the 12th grade examination for B.E. and M.Sc. programmes. • For B.Pharm. and B.E. Environmental and Sustainability Engineering (with PCB input) programmes, a minimum aggregate of 75% marks in Physics, Biology/Mathematics, and Chemistry/Biology/Biotechnology/Technical Vocational subjects with at least 60% marks in each of these subjects in the 12th grade examination. Those who choose Biology as an alternate to Mathematics for applying to B.Pharm. programme must choose from Chemistry/Biotechnology/Technical Vocational subjects as the third subject. • Candidates who have not taken Chemistry in 10+2 curricula will be required to complete bridge course in Chemistry in their first semester. • Candidate should have a minimum aggregate score of 1160 (out of maximum of 1600) in SAT (new format) which includes a Reading & Writing and Mathematics test. • Scores of candidates who had written SAT as per the old format will be mapped using concordance tables available from CollegeBoard (USA). • The candidate should have written the SAT not earlier than February 1, 2024. • Only Students who are appearing for the 12th examination in 2026 or who have passed the 12th Examination in 2025 are eligible. If a candidate has taken more than one attempt in the 12th class or its equivalent, only his/her latest performance is considered. Candidates must meet the following criteria: o Students must appear for their 12th-grade examination for the first time in 2025 or 2026, with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics/Biology as compulsory subjects. OR o Students who completed their 12th-grade examination in 2025 may reappear for improvement exams in specific subject(s). The results of these improvements must be available by the prescribed submission deadline as specified on the admissions portal. OR o Students who retake the full set of 12th-grade subjects are also eligible, provided their results are available by the submission deadline, as specified on the admissions portal. -- 6 of 23 -- Page | 3 Important Notes 1. Admission Process Candidates applying to the undergraduate programmes at BITS Pilani are required to: ▪ Appear for Grade 12 (qualifying examination) and Scholastic Assessment Test (SAT), which includes a Reading & Writing and Mathematics test. ▪ Request CollegeBoard to send SAT scores to BITS Pilani (DI code: 7759–BITS Pilani). ▪ Fill the Application Form online latest by April 05, 2026. The SAT score should be available to the candidates at the time of their application. Candidates should also ensure that their SAT scores must be received by BITS Pilani through CollegeBoard officially latest by April 15, 2026. ▪ Upload required documents such as Grade 12 marks sheets, photographs, copies of passport, etc. If the transcripts of Grade 12 are not available during the first application window, a separate online window to provide Grade 12 marks will be opened and the timeline of the same will be published through admissions website. The passport should be valid for a minimum of six months from the date of joining the institute. ▪ Submit the application and pay the application fee of INR 7000/- online only. ▪ Upon completing the application form online and payment of the application fee online, an acknowledgment will be generated, and candidates should keep this copy of the submitted form and payment details (acknowledgment) with themselves for any future use. Additional or missing information, if any, may be asked by BITS Pilani through email from the candidates. Please quote the application number in all your correspondences related to admissions. ▪ The merit position of all eligible candidates will be prepared based on their SAT scores which include a Reading & Writing and Mathematics test. If there is a tie, it would be eliminated using the following criteria: i. First, the number of years/months of education spent by the candidate in a foreign country (outside India) shall be considered for resolving the tied scores. ii. If the tie still exists, their Mathematics score (out of 800) of SAT exam shall be considered for separating them. iii. If the tie still exists, their Physics, Mathematics, & Chemistry/Biology/Biotechnology/Technical Vocational subjects’ total marks in the 10+2 examination shall be considered for separating them. iv. If the tie still exists, their scores obtained in Mathematics/Biology (Applicable for B.Pharm. programme only) subject in the 12th-grade examination shall be considered for separating them. v. If the tie still exists, their Physics subject scores in the 12th-grade examination shall be considered. vi. If the ties still exist, their Chemistry/Biotechnology/Biology/Technical Vocational subject scores in the 12th-grade examination shall be considered to break the tie. vii. If the tie still exists, preference shall be given to female candidates for separating them. The admission committee reserves the right to impose any further or additional criteria such as conducting the online test, interview of the student, evaluation of extra-curricular activities and exceptional talent, etc., in case of any further tie, which shall be announced if the situation warrants. ▪ Candidates may also be interviewed before offering admission. The related information will be shared with the candidate through email. -- 8 of 23 -- Page | 5 Important Notes ▪ Admission offers for those students who submit the SAT score on or before April 15, 2026, will be announced through the website (https://admissions.bits-pilani.ac.in/ISA/ISA.html) on April 24, 2026 with details of reporting date, scholarships and other requirements and relevant information. Candidates will be given adequate time or 5-10 days to accept the offer by paying the requisite fee. Once the fee is paid, BITS Pilani may then send the printed copy of admission letters to the students requiring applying for VISA. ▪ All information and communication regarding the International Student Admission (ISA) Scheme-2026 admission will be made available to the candidates through the ISA website https://admissions.bits- pilani.ac.in/ISA/ISA.html. Candidates are advised to view this website regularly for up-to-date announcements and all related information for admissions under this scheme. 4.1 FAQs on Admission Process and Eligibility 1) What is SAT and where can I take the SAT Test? • SAT stands for Scholastic Assessment Test and is administered by CollegeBoard, USA. You may refer this link https://satsuite.collegeboard.org/sat/whats-on-the-test for more details. 2) Is the SAT Subject score required for admission? • No, SAT subject score will not be required for admission. As mentioned above, merit position of all eligible candidates will be decided based on their SAT score (new format) and other criteria mentioned above. 3) What is the last SAT sitting that BITS Pilani will accept for applicants? • We suggest that applicants should take SAT tests latest by March 2026. 4) The admission offer will be made based on the latest SAT score or the best of the SAT Scores? • Applicants are suggested to submit their best SAT score by the specified deadline, which will be considered to prepare the merit list for admission. 5) Does BITS Pilani consider SAT superscores? • Yes, the applicants can mention their SAT superscores while filling out the application form and the same may be considered for the admission process. 6) What is the Designated Institution (DI) code of BITS Pilani for SAT? • Designated Institution (DI) code is 7759 – BITS Pilani. 7) When will I hear if I've been admitted? • You will be informed about our admission decision (first list of admission offers) on April 24, 2026 through the International admission website (https://admissions.bits-pilani.ac.in/ISA/ISA.html). Please make sure to check the website regularly for the latest updates. -- 9 of 23 -- Page | 6 8) Does BITS Pilani maintain admission wait-lists? • Yes, BITS Pilani maintains wait-lists. Wait listed students will be also informed through the website. 9) Is an interview part of the selection process? • You may be interviewed before the final decision on admission is made. This interview will not change any merit order of the candidate. However, if the candidate fails to show up for the interview, his/her admission will automatically be canceled. 10) Does BITS Pilani provide scholarships? • Merit-based scholarships are available for all the admitted students in the form of tuition fee waivers which range from 15% to 80%. In the first semester, scholarships will be awarded based on the candidate’s standing in the merit list. Continuation of the scholarship in subsequent semesters will depend on performance of the student at BITS Pilani. 11) What is the medium of instruction at BITS? • All lectures and official communications are in English. 12) What if my results are not available at the time of admission? • Without SAT score your application to BITS Pilani would be incomplete. In case your Grade 12 (qualifying examination) results are not available when you apply, you will be offered provisional admission based on other eligibility criteria. However, you would need to submit the results during the window to submit Grade 12 marks, failing which your admission would be cancelled. 13) Are admissions open to all the four campuses of BITS? • For the academic year 2026-2027, admissions are open at the Pilani, K.K. Birla Goa, and Hyderabad campuses of BITS Pilani. 14) Is it possible for a citizen of a country other than India to choose the admission via either of the intake processes, that is - BITSAT or International Student Admission? • A student who is a citizen of a country other than India can choose to appear for both the modes of admission, that is - BITSAT and International Student Admission (ISA), provided eligibility criteria for each of the modes are met. Through ISA, admissions are open to the Pilani, K.K. Birla Goa, and Hyderabad campuses of BITS Pilani. The timeline for the two modes of admission (BITSAT and ISA) are different. For more details about BITSAT, you may visit: https://admissions.bits-pilani.ac.in. 15) Where is Pilani? • Pilani is located 200 km west of Delhi and 220 km north of Jaipur in the State of Rajasthan and in northwestern part of India. -- 10 of 23 -- Page | 7 16) Where is Goa? • Goa is located in the western region of India; it is bounded by the state of Maharashtra to the north, and by Karnataka to the east and south, while the Arabian Sea forms its western coast. It is India's smallest state by area and the fourth smallest by population. 17) Where is Hyderabad? • Hyderabad, the City of Pearls, is located in the north-western part of the State of Telangana in southeastern India. 18) What about Visa? • Most foreign nationals need a Student Visa to study in India. Integrated Degree Programmes in Bachelor of Engineering, Bachelor of Pharmacy, and Master of Science have several common courses. These degrees are based on a modular structure, and their academic requirements are spelt out in respect of the number of courses and units. All these programmes are structured in such a way that normally a student will be able to finish a programme in eight semesters. The flexibility of the institute allows a student to do their programme at a faster pace and finish it earlier than eight semesters or at a slower pace to finish later than eight semesters. During Practice School (PS), the classroom is shifted to a professional location where the students, under the supervision of the faculty, are involved in applying the knowledge acquired in the classroom for finding solutions to real-life problems. The PS programme consists of two components: PS-I of 2 months’ duration implemented during the summer following the second year and PS-II of 5 ½ months duration, implemented during either of the semesters of the final year. 2) What is the Thesis option? An integrated undergraduate degree programme student must opt for either Thesis or Practice School in their final year of study. In the Thesis option, students will be assigned a topic of research on which they are required to work either at BITS Pilani or at a collaborating organization for duration of five and a half months. 8. Visa India is known for its educational excellence, and it is a popular destination for many international students. International students should obtain a Student Visa valid for the full duration of the course from the Indian Consulates/Embassy situated in their own country. A student would bear the responsibility to ensure that visa should be applied well in advance at the Indian embassy in his/her country. It takes at least three weeks for the Indian Embassy to issue a student visa. BITS Pilani admission letter should be used to obtain student visa. International students taking admission at BITS Pilani should make sure that the student visa is endorsed to BITS Pilani by the visa issuing authority. After entering India, within 14 days, international Students (other than PIO/OCI Card holders) are required to register themselves with the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer (FRRO)/Foreigners Registration Officer (FRO). Office of International Students (OIS), BITS Pilani, will facilitate the Registration. 9.1 FAQs on Visa 1) What is the duration of a Student Visa? ▪ Student Visas are issued for the duration of the academic course of study or for a period of five years, whichever is less, based on letters of admission from BITS Pilani. 2) Where should I apply for a student visa? ▪ You should approach the Indian Embassy/Consulate in your home country to apply for a student visa. -- 15 of 23 -- Page | 12 3) Can a foreign student change his/her Institute/University after coming to India on student Visa? ▪ The name of the Institute/University is to be mentioned while applying for the visa, which is then mentioned on the visa. A request for the change of university or institution subsequently made cannot be considered. In this case a foreign student would need to go back to his/her home country and apply for a new visa. 4) Can BITS Pilani assist in getting student visa? ▪ Student would be responsible to get the student visa. BITS Pilani would issue a letter of admission (after all requirements are met), this letter is to be used for getting the student visa. 10. Life at Pilani Campus BITS Pilani, Pilani Campus is located in the Vidya Vihar campus adjacent to Pilani town in Jhunjhunu district, in Rajasthan. Pilani is the home town of the Birla family and has a population of about 50,000. It is about 200 km west of Delhi and about 220 km north of Jaipur. The Institute buildings, hostels and residential quarters for staff with neatly laid out roads, lawns and gardens constitute the BITS Campus of about 240 acres. CAMPUS AND ITS ADJOINING FACILITIES ➢ Shiv Ganga and Saraswati Temple Shiv Ganga is a central beauty spot of the Vidya Vihar Campus with 400 meters’ circular canal and the Sharda Peeth, a beautiful white marble temple dedicated to Goddess Saraswati. ➢ Guest Accommodation Limited facilities are available for board and lodging on payment at the VFAST Hostel (Visiting Faculty and Students Hostel), which is located near the entrance of the Campus. This apart in the campus, there are lodges and hotels in Pilani town. -- 16 of 23 -- Page | 13 ➢ Shopping Centers AKSHAY, a Supermarket, located in the heart of the campus in an area of 7500 sq.ft. with an elegant modern building is a part of BITS I-5 Consumers’ Cooperative Stores Ltd. (BITS Coop). Student volunteers of the Institute have worked with management of the BITS Coop in the establishment of the Supermarket. ➢ Medical entre Pilani Campus has a Medical Centre, which caters to the medical needs of the students and staff. It has a full time Physician (MD) and a Gynecologist, who attend to the patients both in the morning and evening outdoor hours. A dental surgeon and a Pediatrician visit the centre once in every week. Similarly, the centre also provides services of part time ENT, homeopathy, and Ayurvedic specialists. The Centre has a good clinical laboratory for all major biochemical, hematological, urine, stool and other routine tests. ➢ Birla Museum The Birla Museum is located adjacent to the Institute Building. It is the first science and technology museum established in the country. Most of the exhibits and models incorporate stimulating animations and visual effects. ➢ Central Electronics Engineering Research Institute (CEERI) Adjoining the Campus, there is the Central Electronics Engineering Research Institute. It is one of the National Laboratories under the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR). ➢ Student Housing The Institute is fully residential and hostel accommodation is provided to all students. There is a common kitchen cum mess unit for every set of two boys’ hostels. Each unit of the mess serves vegetarian and non- vegetarian food and the unit operates under the management of different students’ committees. The girls’ hostel, however, has a separate mess of its own, situated within the boundary of the hostel. ➢ Student Activities Centre The Institute has a Student Activities Centre housed in a separate building where students have their union office and rooms for various activities. This building also has badminton courts, a squash court, a Table tennis room, a Health Club, an open air amphitheatre and a cafeteria. ➢ Cultural and Recreational Activities The Institute has following clubs and societies: Music, Dance, Hindi Drama, English Drama, Hindi Press, English Press, Creative Activities, and Mime clubs; English Language Activity and Hindi Activity societies. These are entirely managed by the students and have been nurturing the creative and cultural talents of the students. In addition, the Institute runs Recreational Activity Forum, Photography Club, Swimming Club, and Health Club whose membership is open to students and staff. The Institute also organizes Theatre and Dance workshops. A classical music group called ‘Ragamalika’ aims at encouraging budding talent among the students in music and dance. It also arranges performances by leading artists in the field of classical music and dance. In addition, there is also a BITS Pilani Chapter of SPIC- MACAY which organizes programmes to promote Indian classical music and culture amongst youth. Recreational Activity Forum (RAF) regularly organizes film shows and cultural programmes for the BITS community. BITS being an all- India Institute, students have also established regional associations representing almost all Indian States conducting several special programmes on festive occasions. -- 17 of 23 -- Page | 14 ➢ Physical Education Physical Education of the Institute aims at providing a safe atmosphere to enable students and staff members to exercise to their potential whilst achieving their goals. It offers a variety of fitness, wellness, and recreation opportunities, and Fitness Programmes including Yoga and Martial Arts. The Physical Education has major facilities that include Health Club, Swimming Club and Sports Club. Health Club is equipped with single and multi-stationed machines and weight training facilities to provide students with an opportunity of doing exercise for physical fitness. Swimming Club has a swimming pool of 25 m length while Sports Club has various indoor and outdoor facilities for students to take part in sports and games. The indoor facilities are Badminton, Table Tennis and Squash with synthetic flooring while outdoor facilities are Basketball, Football, Hockey, Volleyball, Cricket, Tennis, Track & Field (400 m) etc. Sports and fitness activities are supervised by the qualified and experienced staff members of the Institute. ➢ Festivals on Campus Traditionally students organize three festivals during an academic year. BOSM (BITS Open Sports Meet) in September, a sports festival; OASIS, a cultural festival in October and APOGEE (A Professions-Oriented Gathering Over Educational Experience), an Academic Festival in February thus bringing about a beautiful blend of sports, cultural and academic milieu of the campus. All the three festivals are entirely managed by students in which a large number of students from all over India actively participate. 10.1 FAQs on Life at Pilani Campus 1) Would my electrical device work in India? ▪ The power in India is 230volt and 50 Hz; you may need an adapter for your device. 2) Would my cell phone work in India? ▪ Mobile phones in India operate using GSM technology and function within 900/1800 MHz ranges. RMIT Classification: Trusted BITS-RMIT Higher Education Academy © BITSAT-2026, Birla Institute of Technology & Science, Pilani -- 1 of 8 -- I RMIT Classification: Trusted BITS-RMIT Higher Education Academy Information BITS Pilani (an Institution of Eminence in India) has entered a partnership with RMIT University, Australia, to develop a Higher Education Academy called BITS-RMIT Higher Education Academy. The BITS-RMIT Academy offers collaborative degree programmes at the international level. Students admitted under this collaboration will have the unique opportunity to immerse themselves in diverse cultures and gain a truly global perspective. In this 4-year collaborative ‘dual degree’ programme, students will spend the first two years along with a summer term at BITS Pilani campuses before getting transferred to RMIT campuses in Australia for the remaining two years (i.e., years 3 and 4) of their study period. Our innovative curriculum combines the strengths of both academic environments, offering an outstanding education that would preparethem for success in today’s rapidly changing world. With state-of-the-art facilities, inspiring faculty, and a wide range of extracurricular activities, this collaboration would be the perfect place to launch students’ productive academic and professional journeys. It is planned to admit students in the following four undergraduate programmes from two leading universities from the Academic Year 2026-27 programmes onward. • Bachelor of Engineering (Civil and Infrastructure) (Honours) by RMIT and B.E. Civil by BITS Pilani, Pilani Campus • Bachelor of Engineering (Mechanical Engineering) (Honours) by RMIT and B.E. Mechanical by BITS Pilani, Pilani Campus • Bachelor of Engineering (Electronic & Computer Systems Engineering) (Honours) by RMIT and B.E. Electronics and Communication by BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus • Bachelor of Engineering (Electrical Engineering) (Honours) by RMIT and B.E. Electrical and Electronics by BITS Pilani, Hyderabad Campus • Bachelor of Engineering (Software Engineering) (Honours) by RMIT and B.E. Computer Science by BITS Pilani, K K Birla Goa Campus • Bachelor of Computer Science by RMIT and B.E. Computer Science by BITS Pilani, K K Birla Goa Campus -- 2 of 8 -- II RMIT Classification: Trusted 1. Eligibility Requirement for Admission: The eligibility requirement for admission to all the six programmes offered by BITS- RMIT Academy mentioned above are given as under: Admissions will be made purely on merit. The merit position of the candidate for admission will be based on the score obtained by the candidate in the BITSAT-2026. Thus, it is essential that applicant undertakes the BITS Admission Test (BITSAT) and achieves a score that meets or exceeds the relevant cut-off score for admission to the BITS-RMIT programmes. In addition to BITSAT score, applicant must also fulfil the minimum eligibility requirement for admission prescribed by both BITS Pilani and RMIT Australia as mentioned below. (a) BITS Pilani minimum eligibility requirement Applicant should also fulfil the minimum eligibility requirement of BITS Pilani for admission as follows: (i) The applicant has passed the 12th examination of 10+2 system from a recognized Central or State board or its equivalent with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (PCM) and adequate proficiency in English; Also, the applicant has obtained a minimum of aggregate 75% marks in PCM in 12th examination, with at least 60% marks in each of the PCM subjects. (ii) The applicant undertakes the BITS Admission Test (BITSAT) and achieves a score that meets or exceeds the relevant cut-off score for admission to the BITS Award, as determined by BITS from time to time. (b) RMIT Australia minimum eligibility requirement Applicant should also fulfil the minimum eligibility requirement of RMIT Australia for admission as follows: (i) One of the following must be achieved: Successful completion of one of the following secondary qualifications in India: -- 3 of 8 -- III RMIT Classification: Trusted 1. All India Senior School Certificate (AISSC) 10+2 with a minimum average of 65%* 2. Indian School Certificate (ISC) with a minimum average of 65%* 3. State Boards of Education Higher Secondary Certificate, (HSC) with a minimum average of 70%* *Overall average for graded academic subjects, excluding work experience, physical and health education, art, religious and general studies. (ii) Successful completion of the AISSC; ISC; State Board HSC Mathematics/ HSC Mathematics with a minimum grade of 60%. (iii) Where an applicant does not have an Indian secondary qualification, they must meet the RMIT criteria for their respective country of secondary education study as approved by RMIT and notified to BITS by RMIT (listed on the RMIT website under entry requirements by country, from time to time). (iv) English Language Entry Requirements Applicants can provide evidence of your English language proficiency for admission to BITS RMIT Higher Education Academy program from one of these options: • A secondary qualification completed in English with the minimum achieved score AND an official letter from said school confirming your Year 12 studies were taught and assessed entirely in English. OR • An English Language proficiency test The minimum scores to achieve to meet RMIT’s English Language proficiency requirements as follows: 1. Achieved 70% or above in Year 12 English subject score in Indian School Certificate examination (ISC) * 2. Achieved 75% or above in Year 12 English subject score in Central Board of Senior Education examination (CBSE) * If applicants have other secondary qualifications or do not meet the subject score requirements listed above they will need to provide English language proficiency tests results. RMIT accepts a range of English proficiency tests. Refer to English -- 4 of 8 -- IV RMIT Classification: Trusted language proficiency tests for international students website for the list of acceptable tests and scores required for admission** (*) You must provide an official letter from your high school office confirming that your Year 12 studies were taught and assessed entirely in English. For detailed information on English language requirements and other proficiency tests recognised by the Academy, including validity periods, visit English language requirements and equivalency information. RMIT will reimburse 50% of the English proficiency test cost up to a maximum value of 8500 INR, for any candidates who are successfully enrolled into an Academy program in 2026 intake. Where an English language proficiency test is used for admission, the test must be taken no more than 2 years prior to the applicant’s Commencing Date for the Academy Program and will need to be supplied to RMIT by the deadline as published in BITS Pilani Admission website.
